Accurately transcribe and enter key data points into our CRM system, including: Project Documentation: Transcribing general field notes, structural observations, and pre-existing property conditions. Labor Tracking: Logging precise project start and stop times to maintain accurate job-costing metrics. Chemical Application Logs: Recording exact chemical mixes used on site (e.g., Sodium Hypochlorite ratios, surfactants, or specialized neutralizers) and tracking raw material consumption. I ---------- & Safety Tracking: Review field sheets for any reported field anomalies, near-misses, or equipment failures. Extract and log this critical data into our dedicated i ---------- and a ---------- management tracking tool to support our proactive risk-mitigation protocols. Lead Management & Inbound Nurturing: Monitor incoming leads arriving in the CRM database. Manage initial client touchpoints exclusively via professional text and email communication (no voice calls required) to qualify leads and guide them cleanly into our bidding pipeline. 2. Social Media Creation & Daily Management Daily Multi-Platform Posting: Execute a rigorous, daily posting schedule across platforms critical to the Washington D.C. Metro market (Facebook , Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, and YouTube Shorts). Video Engineering & Editing: Take raw, unedited footage of satisfying cleaning sequences (before/after transformations, drone flight lines, surface cleaning arcs) and cut them into pristine, high-impact vertical videos (9:16) using tools like CapCut, Adobe Premiere, or DaVinci Resolve. Media Annotation & Value Inlays: Add clean, professional text overlays, captioning, trending audio tracks, and graphic callouts (using Canva and advanced video effects) that educate the audience on how and why we clean scientifically. Local Brand Positioning: Tailor captions and hashtags to resonate with property managers, HOAs, commercial real estate developers, and high-end homeowners in the Northern Virginia, D.C., and Maryland corridors. 3. Brand Safety & Technical Integrity Gatekeeping PPE & OSHA Compliance Review: Review all raw field footage prior to editing to guarantee our brand exhibits 100% safety compliance. You will actively screen out any footage showing technicians violating safety protocols (e.g., missing eye/face protection, improper respirator use during chemical transfer, or lack of fall protection/harnesses on roof pitches). You will be trained by our leadership to distinguish between high-pressure blasting and low-pressure chemical softwashing, ensuring captions accurately explain how our chemical applications safely eliminate organic contaminants down to the spore without damaging delicate building materials. Required Skills & Experience Data Integrity & Speed: Exceptional accuracy and speed in data entry. Ability to read handwritten or scanned field worksheets and carefully extract technical data without errors. Software Mastery: Proficient in CapCut (or professional equivalent video editor) and Canva for rapid, high-quality asset design. CRM Familiarity: Proven experience navigating small business CRM frameworks, pipeline management, and client communication workflows. Visual Storytelling Eye: An exceptional eye for rhythm, color correction, and pacing in video editing—specifically maximizing the "oddly satisfying" nature of exterior cleaning transformations. Flawless Written English: Perfect command of English grammar and professional tone. Ability to write sophisticated captions for commercial property managers as well as engaging, punchy copy for residential homeowners. Operational Reliability: A rock-solid remote working infrastructure, including a high-spec editing computer, lightning-fast internet, and a reliable power/internet backup solution to maintain daily consistency. I'm a neuropsychologist by training, an entrepreneur by passion, and a wife and mom of two by the grace of God. I've been working with an outside agency for our Meta ads, and after a thorough look at the numbers, I'm bringing this work in house. I want someone embedded with our brand who knows our voice, our funnels, and our audience the way only an in house partner can. I have a launch in August and ongoing evergreen lead generation that needs steady hands. So I'm hiring my Meta Ads Manager. Who You'd Be Helping My audience is ambitious women who are smart, driven, and quietly tired. They're moms, entrepreneurs, executives, and creatives who've built impressive lives and want to keep building with their nervous systems intact. My content gives them practical systems backed by neuroscience and softened by faith and grace. My brand sits at the intersection of productivity, neuroscience, and faith based personal development. Knowing how this audience thinks and what they respond to is half the job here. What You'd Own You'd run the entire Meta ads program. Here's how that breaks down. Strategy and structure You'd build campaign structure for both launches and evergreen lead generation. You'd design the audience targeting, set up the creative testing framework, and pace the budget across the month. Launch campaigns For each course launch (next one is August 2026), you'd plan the full ad sequence from awareness through close. You'd brief the creative needs, pull copy from our organic content, and run the creative testing during the launch window. Evergreen funnels You'd run ongoing top of funnel ads to grow our email list and book launch waitlist. You'd watch the funnel metrics, identify what's working, and shift budget toward winners. Reporting Each week, you'd send a short performance summary covering spend, results by campaign, what changed, and what you're testing next. A clean weekly note in Slack or Notion is all I need. Coordination You'd work alongside our Content Producer who handles organic YouTube and Instagram. They produce the creative assets and on brand visuals. You take what's working in organic and turn it into ad creative that converts. Who You Probably Are You live inside Meta Ads Manager. You know the platform deeply, including the dashboard quirks, the policy gotchas, and how to read the data underneath the surface metrics. You've run ads for creators, coaches, or boutique brands in the $3K to $20K per month spend range. You understand that small spend takes a different kind of thinking than enterprise spend. You've supported at least 3 to 5 course launches end to end. You know what the launch funnel looks like, how to brief creative, and how to manage budget pacing across the open cart window. You take deadlines seriously. When you say something will be done by Friday, it's done by Friday. If something comes up, you flag it early. You're warm and direct. You can give and receive feedback without ego. You ask good questions and you don't make excuses. You've got at least 3 years of Meta ads experience with real budget responsibility. Bonus if you've worked with personal brands or creator businesses. A Note On AI AI works as a tool inside your process. The campaign architecture, the creative strategy, and the funnel logic come from your brain. AI is fine for headline variations, copy ideation, or speeding up your creative testing iteration. The thinking that sits underneath the ad account has to be yours. Tools We'll Use Meta Ads Manager, Klaviyo for email , Notion for reporting and project management, Slack for daily communication, and Google Drive for asset sharing. What I'm Offering You'll have flexibility on your hours and schedule. Outside of agreed deadlines and meetings, you run your own day. You'll work in a trust based environment. I don't micromanage. I set clear expectations and trust you to deliver. There's real growth potential here. As the brand grows toward our September 2027 book launch, your role and pay can grow with it. I want the right person to be here for the long haul. You'll be part of a creative partnership rooted in something deeper than hustle. The content we make helps women all over the world build calmer, more aligned lives. Compensation Compensation will be discussed during the interview process. I'm open to hourly, or flat monthly retainer depending on what works best for both sides. How This Starts We'll start with a 30 day paid trial focused on auditing the current account, mapping the August launch plan, and running our first week of campaigns together. If we both feel the fit, we'll extend into a longer engagement. To Apply Fill out the application form here: ---------- One question will ask if there's anything else you'd like me to know. description: Updated Description: Senior EA / Operations VA for US Medical Consulting Firm — Policy & SOP Review, Notion, Long-Term I have updated the description from my prior job posting, and including questions specifically related to QBO, Outlook, Zapier, Notion, and Healthcare experience. I'm a physician and medical director based in Colorado, US. I own a single-physician PLLC that provides medical director services and NP/PA supervision to clinics across multiple US states (IV hydration, med spa, aesthetics, GLP-1, primary care). I'm hiring one senior person to own the day-to-day operations so I can focus on the medical, compliance, and growth side of the business. This is a long-term, embedded role. If you're looking for a 3-month gig, this isn't it. If you're looking for a business owner you can grow with for years, we may be a good fit. What you'll own Policy and SOP review. I have a library of clinic policies, standing orders, supervision agreements, and internal SOPs that support a multi-state practice. I will need you to review them, flag gaps, track versions, and propose edits. You don't need to be a lawyer or clinician, just be willing and able to look up normal policies and compare. Inbox monitoring and drafting. I get 30 to 60 inbound email s per day. Most are noise; a few are real new-client inquiries, state board notices, or NP/PA collaboration requests. You'll triage, draft responses in my voice for me to approve, and surface what actually needs my attention. Calendar and scheduling. Managing my availability across consults, clinic onboardings, and personal time. Occasional client text messages. Same voice-matching skill as email , lower volume. Client and CRM organization. Keeping records of every clinic, NP, and PA I work with, including contract status, state, audit cadence, supervision agreement renewal dates. This will likely be an automated process we'll be building around; I'm hiring a contractor to build us a program from the ground up. Google Drive cleanup and ongoing structure. 1.5 years of accumulated documents across multiple state PLLCs need a clean folder taxonomy with naming conventions and version control. Filtering inbound offers. New clinic inquiries, NP/PA collaboration requests, vendor pitches, and partnership offers come in regularly. You'll triage these against a checklist I'll teach you, surface the real opportunities, and bring the ones with potential to my attention. Eventually: light QuickBooks Online work, basic AP/AR and invoicing for the PLLC. Training provided if you don't have QBO experience but understand bookkeeping fundamentals. Tools we use - Notion (primary source of truth, must have hands-on experience, not just exposure) - Zapier (current automations; willing to train someone strong who hasn't used it yet) - Google Workspace (Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Docs, Sheets) - Microsoft Outlook and Calendar - QuickBooks Online (training provided if you have bookkeeping fundamentals) - ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity (AI assistance is encouraged, not banned) What I'm looking for - 2+ years of real EA or operations VA experience supporting US-based founders, executives, or business owners - Strong written English, you'll be drafting in my voice and writing to physicians, attorneys, and clinic owners - Comfortable in healthcare-adjacent work (HIPAA awareness expected; clinical background not required but a plus) - Proactive, you flag issues early and propose solutions, you don't wait to be asked - Organized to the point of being a little annoying about it (this is a compliment) - Discreet, you'll see sensitive business and patient-adjacent information - Available long-term, full-time, with at least some overlap with US business hours preferred Who you are not - Looking for project-based or short-term work - A pure social media manager, content creator, or copywriter (those skills are nice but not the job) - Hoping to grow into a clinical role (this is admin-first and will stay that way) - A generalist who'll need everything explained from scratch, I want someone who walks in with judgment How to apply Send me a message that includes all four of the following. Applications that skip any of these will not be reviewed: 1. Briefly tell me about yourself, not a resume dump, just who you are and why this role caught your eye. 2. Walk me through how you'd approach the first 30 days of inbox triage for someone like me, assuming you have access to my inbox and a brief intro to my business. What would you set up first? 3. Explicitly state your hands-on experience with each of the following. For each one, tell me how many years you've used it, what you've actually done with it, and rate yourself: none, basic, intermediate, or advanced. Don't lump them together, give me one line per item. - EA or operations VA experience (years supporting US-based founders, executives, or business owners; lead clients you've worked with) - QuickBooks Online - Microsoft Outlook - Zapier - Notion - Healthcare or HIPAA-adjacent work 4. One question you have for me. Anyone who asks zero questions about the role isn't curious enough for this hire. I read every application that follows these instructions, and I'll respond within 3 business days to candidates I think would be a good match. Looking forward to hearing from you. — Thomas

If I say "I'm flying to Buenos Aires tomorrow," I don't want you to ask "what do you need?" — I want you to immediately start thinking about airport transfer, hotel check-in time, local SIM card, dinner options, and what the weather will be like. Someone who communicates clearly and honestly. If you don't know something — say so. If you can't verify information — tell me. I'd rather hear "I couldn't confirm this" than get made-up answers. Someone who is comfortable messaging real businesses. You'll be contacting restaurants, hotels, gyms, barbershops, laundry services, clinics, and other providers via WhatsApp, Instagram DM, email , and occasionally phone — on my behalf, every day. WHAT YOU'LL DO (examples of real tasks): — Research and book restaurants based on my preferences (cuisine, vibe, location, price) — Find and set up local services when I arrive in a new city: gym, barber, laundry, coworking space, coffee shops — Handle hotel communication: bookings, early check-in requests, complaints, follow-ups — Organize travel logistics: flights, airport transfers, eSIM/SIM cards, visa requirements, packing reminders — Manage a weekly budget for personal expenses and track spending — Send messages to businesses and follow up if they don't reply — Set up recurring reminders and systems so nothing falls through the cracks — Research and compare options (e.g., "find me 3 good gyms near my apartment with day passes") — Keep a shared task log and send a daily update every evening TOOLS WE USE: — Telegram (primary communication — must be available and responsive) — Google Sheets (task tracking and expense logging) — Google Maps (research and finding places) — Google Calendar (scheduling and reminders) — WhatsApp and Instagram (messaging businesses) — Airbnb and ---------- (travel research) REQUIREMENTS: — Strong written and spoken English — Available on Telegram during work hours with fast response time (under 30 min) — Reliable internet connection — Comfortable making real research — using Google Maps, checking Instagram pages, verifying opening hours, finding real links — Honest and transparent — if something goes wrong, tell me immediately — Previous VA or PA experience preferred but not required if you're sharp and motivated — NOT looking for someone who copy-pastes from ChatGPT and pretends it's research WORK SCHEDULE: Flexible — we'll agree on your hours based on your availability and my time zone. I care about results, not sitting at a desk at exact times. You'll send a daily update every working day so we both know what's done and what's pending. PAYMENT: $5/hour, paid weekly. Payment via Wise, PayPal, or USDT — your choice. Opportunity to grow into a full-time role with higher pay if we work well together. HOW TO APPLY: Do NOT send me your resume or a generic cover letter. I will not read it. Send me a message with the word READY and I will reply with a link to a short screening test. The test takes about 30 minutes and includes real tasks similar to what you'd do in this role. I review every completed test personally. If you're a strong match, I'll message you on Telegram within a few days. Applications without a completed test will not be considered.

I run a YouTube channel called Wii Explained, focused on nostalgic and entertaining videos about the Nintendo Wii, Wii channels, Wii accessories, knockoffs, and other retro gaming topics. I’m looking for a video editor who can closely match my current editing style and help improve it even more. What I’m looking for You need to be able to: Recreate the exact style of my current videos Edit for high retention, not just basic cuts Understand English voice-over clearly and match visuals to what is being said Have a strong sense of visual rhythm and pacing Add smooth moving images, zooms, effects, pop-ups, transitions, and visual jokes Make the video feel nostalgic, clean, and entertaining Keep the edit flowing so viewers don’t get bored I especially want more moving visuals and effects like in the first 30 seconds of my newest video, “The Weirdest Wii Channels”, but even smoother and more polished. Assets I will provide I will provide: The full voice-over Some Wii images and video clips when needed My Mii mascot in different poses Notes about the video style and structure We can discuss whether you will also help search for extra images/videos yourself. Some Wii footage or images may be provided by me because they need to be accurate or untouched. Style The videos should feel: Nostalgic Funny, but not over-edited Smooth and easy to watch Similar to my current channel style Focused on viewer retention This is not just basic editing. I need someone who understands timing, movement, and how to make a voice-over visually interesting. Requirements Must understand English well Must understand what the voice-over is saying Must be able to match visuals to the script Must be able to follow an existing style closely Experience with YouTube editing is preferred Retro gaming / Nintendo / Wii knowledge is a plus Budget My budget is $25–$50 per video, negotiable depending on quality, speed, and how much work you can take off my hands. I’m looking to produce around 1 video per week, so this can become long-term work if we work well together. How to apply Please answer these questions: What editing program do you use? How much experience do you have with YouTube video editing? Can you recreate an existing editing style from a reference video? Do you understand English voice-overs well? Are you comfortable editing nostalgic / gaming content? Can you help search for images and clips if needed? How fast can you usually deliver one video? Please send examples of videos you edited, preferably YouTube-style content. Next Step If your application looks good, you will move on to the next round. To make sure you read the full post, start your application with: “Wii Editor”

title: n8n / API Developer for FieldPulse + CTM + AI Voice Intake Automation
job_title: n8n / API Developer for FieldPulse + CTM + AI Voice Intake Automation
description: Project Overview I am looking for an experienced automation/API developer to build Phase 1 of a field service intake automation system. This project involves CallTrackingMetrics, FieldPulse, n8n, webhooks, APIs, customer lookup, job creation, alerts, and AI voice intake. The goal of Phase 1 is not full dispatch or scheduling. The goal is to create a reliable intake system that captures qualified service requests, creates or updates the correct customer/job record, and sends alerts so a human can review and take over. Phase 1 Scope The first build should include these modules: Module 1 — Intake / Webhook Receiver Receive incoming call/contact/intake data through webhook or API. This may come from CallTrackingMetrics, an AI voice agent, web form, chatbot, or test payload. The workflow should capture and structure fields such as: Customer name Phone number Service location / city / ZIP Vehicle or equipment description Service issue Urgency Roadside / safety status if applicable Lead source / tracking number if available Call summary or transcript if available Module 2 — AI Voice Intake Assistant Set up or integrate an AI voice intake assistant that collects required intake information. The voice agent must act only as an intake assistant. It should not diagnose, estimate, schedule, dispatch, or promise response times. The voice agent should identify whether the caller is a qualified service request, out of area, sales/spam, existing customer follow-up, or needs human follow-up. Module 3 — FieldPulse Customer / Job Record Creation Use FieldPulse API or approved integration method to: Search for an existing customer before creating a new one Avoid duplicate customer records when possible Create or update customer information Create a job, lead, or service request record Attach relevant intake details, notes, call summary, source, and urgency Module 4 — Alerts and Human Review Output Send alerts when a qualified service request is received. Minimum alert output should include: Customer name Phone number City / ZIP / location Vehicle or equipment Service issue Urgency Roadside / safety status FieldPulse customer/job link if available Intake summary Whether the record was created, updated, or flagged for review Alerts may be sent by SMS, email , FieldPulse notification, or another agreed method. Important Rules This is Phase 1 only. The system should not automatically dispatch technicians, schedule appointments, give price estimates, diagnose mechanical problems, order parts, or promise arrival times. Human review remains part of the process. Required Experience Please apply only if you have experience with some or all of the following: n8n workflow automation Webhooks and REST APIs CRM or field-service software API integrations Customer lookup before creating new records Job, lead, or service request creation through API CallTrackingMetrics, FieldPulse, or similar platforms AI voice agents such as Vapi, Retell, Twilio, Bland, or similar Error handling, logging, and workflow documentation Preferred First Step I would like to start with a small fixed-price test module before the full build. The test module should prove that you can receive a sample intake payload, apply qualification logic, check for an existing customer, prepare a FieldPulse-ready record, and send a structured alert. Please include in your response: Relevant n8n/API/webhook projects you have built Whether you have worked with FieldPulse, CallTrackingMetrics, or similar platforms Whether you have built AI voice intake agents Your recommended approach for Phase 1 Estimated hours and cost for the first test module

description: CS & SALES SPECIALIST - HYBRID ROLE (REMOTE) Wheels, Tires & Accessories ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY We are a fast-growing online wheels and tires retailer built around lease-to-own and installment financing. We help customers across the US get the setup they want on their vehicle today and pay over time - and we do it primarily through text, call, and email . We're looking for a sharp, people-first communicator to join our team as a Customer Service (CS) & Sales Specialist. This is a fully remote, phone and text-based role where you'll be handling both new sales conversations and existing order support. If you're someone who's great on the phone, catches on fast, and likes earning more when you perform - keep reading. WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING You'll be the first point of contact for customers reaching out through our store line via call or text. On any given day that means: - Helping new customers find the right wheels and tires for their vehicle (we have tools that make fitment easy - no prior automotive expertise required) - Walking customers through our financing and lease-to-own options and helping them get approved - Handling inbound questions about existing orders - tracking, delivery, reassurance - Following up with warm leads (approved customers who haven't checked out yet, abandoned carts, denied applications) - Confirming order details and flagging anything that needs attention - Redirecting complex support issues through the right channels so nothing falls through the cracks This is not a cold-calling role. Every conversation is inbound or a warm follow-up. COMPENSATION Base Pay: $5.00/hr On top of base, here's where it gets interesting: - $10.00 per sale you were meaningfully involved in closing (we're generous with attribution - if you played a real part in the sale, it counts) - $10.00 bonus for every 5 sales closed by you in a single work week - Store-wide performance bonuses when the team is hitting strong numbers overall - we believe in sharing the win The base is intentionally modest because the commission and bonus structure is where the real earning happens. Reps who are active, consistent, and good at following up earn significantly more than the hourly rate alone. You're also welcome to work after hours if you want to close more sales and earn more commission - we allow this and support it. After-hours CS work that falls outside commission territory is also tracked and we do our best to compensate fairly. Pay is sent every Friday, on time, every week. SCHEDULE AND PLATFORM Platform: Quo (formerly OpenPhone) - calls and texts managed from one inbox Shift A: Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM EST Shift B: Monday to Friday, 3 PM to 9 PM EST + Saturday and Sunday 9 AM to 3 PM EST You're welcome to work beyond your scheduled shift for additional commission. On slower after-hours stretches where no sales come through, we do our best to recognize that extra effort. Call logic: First available rep answers the store line. Text logic: Conversations are assigned to specific reps to keep relationships consistent. Reps can assist each other's conversations - just coordinate internally so two reps don't message the same customer at the same time. TOOLS YOU'LL USE - Quo / OpenPhone - calls, texts, inbox management - Shopify - pulling up orders, verifying customer details - AI fitment tools - checking wheel and tire compatibility for customer vehicles (we provide full training on this) - Our customer-facing website - product pages, cart, checkout flow - Lender portals - checking approval statuses across multiple financing partners No prior experience with these tools is required. We provide full onboarding and an extremely comprehensive set of SOPs, scripts, and paste-ins so you're never winging it. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - Strong communicator - professional, warm, and clear on both calls and texts - Detail-oriented - you read carefully and follow protocols without cutting corners - Self-directed - you can manage your own queue, prioritize correctly, and stay on top of follow-ups without being micromanaged - Coachable - you take feedback well and actually apply it - Reliable - you show up for your shift and don't leave conversations hanging Prior sales or customer service experience is a plus. Prior automotive knowledge is not required - the tools and SOPs handle the technical side. Anyone motivated can learn this quickly. HOW IT WORKS DAY TO DAY You'll work from a shared inbox. Inbound calls and texts come in through the store line and get handled or triaged based on what the customer needs. Sales questions get worked through scripts and financing tools. Quick support questions get answered directly - anything more complex gets routed to the right channel. Warm leads get followed up on a structured schedule. Everything is documented, recorded, and reviewed daily and weekly. We audit calls and texts for quality and give real feedback - not just to catch mistakes but to help you earn more. If you're ever unsure about something on a call, you put the customer on a brief hold, look it up in the SOP, or check with the manager. We'd rather you take 30 seconds to get the right answer than give a wrong one. We have the resources to handle almost any situation - you just need to know where to look. HOW YOU'LL RAMP UP We don't throw you into the deep end. New reps go through a structured onboarding before handling live conversations. During training, we'll connect via Microsoft Teams, calls, and text - so you'll always have a direct line to get questions answered and feedback in real time. Week 1: Learn the SOPs, tools, scripts, and how the business works. You'll shadow real conversations before handling any. Week 2: Start on inbound texts only - lower-stakes, written, and easier to review. You'll get real feedback before moving forward. Week 3+: Sales texts and inbound calls once you're comfortable and consistent. This is where commission starts stacking. Eventually: Customer service responsibilities are added for reps who've demonstrated reliability, judgment, and follow-through. CS access is earned, not assumed. The ramp exists because we'd rather you be confident and accurate than fast and wrong. Most reps are handling a full workload within their first month. ESCALATION BOUNDARIES - WHAT'S NOT YOUR JOB You handle sales, fitment, financing guidance, and order reassurance. You do not handle: - Refund approvals (routed to support email ) - Cancellations (routed to support email ) - Damage claims without shipping protection (routed to support email ) - Order processing or fulfillment (Operations Manager only) - Financing account issues (routed directly to lender) These have clear escalation paths built into every script. You'll always know exactly where to send something. GROWTH AND PROMOTIONS This role has a real growth path for the right person. Reps who perform consistently, follow protocols, and show leadership instincts are considered first when senior rep and lead positions open up. We promote from within when we can - the people who know the operation best are the ones we want running more of it. TO APPLY Send your application message directly through OnlineJobs.ph. Please include: 1. A short video (60 to 90 seconds) of yourself speaking in English. Talk about your background, why this role interests you, and what reliable means to you in a remote work setting. No scripts - we want to hear how you actually communicate. Upload your video to Loom, YouTube (unlisted), or Google Drive and paste the link in your message. 2. A few sentences about what you are looking for long-term. We are not hiring for a short contract or a side gig - we want someone who wants to grow with us. Applications without a video will not be reviewed. What we're looking for in that video: - Neutral, easy-to-follow English - our customers are everyday Americans and need to understand you clearly and comfortably on a call - Confidence and warmth - how you speak matters as much as what you say - Someone who sounds like they actually want this, not just any remote job 100% of calls and texts are recorded for training and quality assurance. By applying you acknowledge that all communications on the store line are monitored.

What this involves: - Working from a set of standard reference drawings that we'll provide. - For each one, producing matched sets — a reference version that follows the source standard exactly, plus several variations of it that deliberately deviate from the standard in specific, controlled ways. - Each plan must be produced in AutoCAD at actual scale, with the DXF model space in feet. The geometry must match the labels: if a distance is labeled "320 ft," the measured distance between the relevant sign insertion points in the DXF must equal 320 ft. This is the most important requirement of the project — many drafters label distances without actually drawing them to scale, and that won't work here. - For each plan, also producing a sidecar annotation file (JSON) recording the key dimensions used and, for the deviating versions, what was changed and where (with DXF coordinates). - Final output per plan: a layered DXF file in feet, plus the matching JSON file. Trial: We start with a small paid batch (6 plans from a single source). If the work is good, we scale up significantly from there — hundreds of plans over the following months. Pricing structure: - The 6-plan trial: paid at an agreed rate. - After the trial, the next ~10–15 plans are paid hourly while you build templates and internalize the workflow. - Once you're producing plans steadily, we switch to a per-plan rate based on your actual time during the hourly phase. The per-plan rate is structured so your effective hourly earnings stay higher than during ramp-up — efficient work pays off. Requirements: - Strong AutoCAD proficiency. Comfortable working in DXF/DWG with model-space units in feet, and you understand block insertion points. - Ability to read technical standards and apply them precisely — looking up values in tables, following the right formulas for the right cases. - Attention to detail. Geometry must match labels exactly. We will verify by measuring the DXF. - Comfortable producing structured JSON files alongside CAD output. - Good English communication. Helpful but not required: - Prior experience with traffic control plans, work zone drawings, or U.S.-style roadway standards. How to apply: 1. Share a sample of CAD work where the geometry is drawn to actual scale — ideally a traffic or roadway-related plan, but any precision engineering CAD is fine. 2. Tell us your hourly rate. 3. Estimated turnaround for the 6-plan trial. 4. In 2–3 sentences, confirm you understand the "geometry must match labels at actual scale in DXF model space" requirement and how you'd verify it before delivery. Applications that don't address point 4 will not be considered.

title: Account Manager - Business Funding
description: Verna Capital is a high-growth business funding consultancy. We help ambitious entrepreneurs, real estate investors, and e-commerce operators secure the capital they need to scale—primarily through 0% interest credit card stacking, lines of credit, SBA loans, and alternative financing. We operate differently than the rest of the funding space. We don't push products based on commission; we build custom, bank-by-bank funding strategies based on our clients' actual credit profiles and business needs. We are consultative, relationship-driven, and highly structured. As we scale, we are looking for a sharp, detail-obsessed Business Funding Account Manager to take ownership of our fulfillment pipeline and become the primary point of contact for our clients post-sale. The Role This is not a passive "check-in" customer success role. You are the operator who takes the baton from our sales team, analyzes the client's credit profile, builds their funding game plan, and guides them through the application process to secure maximum capital. You will manage a capped book of 30 active clients (quality over volume), ensuring every client moves smoothly through our 8-stage pipeline from onboarding to post-approval capital maximization. What You Will Do •Client Intake & Onboarding: Take immediate handoff from sales, send welcome materials, pull credit reports, and run the onboarding call to set expectations. •Credit Analysis & Strategy: Read full tri-bureau credit reports to identify utilization issues, inquiries, and fundability blockers. Build custom, sequenced funding game plans based on current bank rules and underwriting criteria. •Application Execution: Run live application sessions with clients via Zoom or TeamViewer. Ensure flawless, batch-submitted applications with zero mismatched data points. •Pipeline Management: Own the client status board in our CRM. Ensure no client goes silent for more than 3 days. Surface pipeline risks, stuck clients, and escalations to leadership weekly. •Client Communication: Serve as the single point of contact. Hold strict response time SLAs (24 hours Mon-Fri). Handle hard conversations cleanly, including denials, low limits, and expectation resets. •Post-Approval Maximization: Run post-approval calls to review limits, APRs, and 0% promo terms. Coach clients on optimal card usage, collect testimonials, and identify upsell opportunities for future funding rounds. •Process Improvement: Surface gaps in our SOPs, help refine internal workflows, and eventually help train future Account Managers as we grow the team. What Success Looks Like •30 Days: Fully onboarded, shadowing all calls, game plan templates internalized, and our internal knowledge base read end-to-end. •60 Days: Running onboarding and game plan calls solo, executing applications via TeamViewer, and managing 10+ active clients. •90 Days: Full pipeline ownership for all post-sale clients, maintaining a 90%+ on-time response SLA, collecting your first batch of testimonials, and actively contributing to SOP improvements. Required Skills & Experience •2+ years in a client-facing Account Manager, Customer Success, or high-touch operations role at a service business. •Demonstrated ability to manage 20+ active client relationships simultaneously without dropping the ball. •Excellent written and verbal communication—capable of handling calls, email s, and texts at a highly professional level. •Comfortable with screen-share and remote tools (Zoom, TeamViewer, Loom, Google Workspace). •CRM proficiency (GoHighLevel, Monday.com, HubSpot, or similar). •Self-managed and capable of working independently without daily handholding. Strongly Preferred •Background in finance, lending, credit, or business funding. •Experience working with credit reports, FICO scores, and underwriting concepts. •Prior exposure to credit card stacking, business funding, SBA, or commercial lending. •Experience running client-facing calls in a coaching or done-for-you service business. Who Should NOT Apply •Anyone who needs a script for every conversation. •Anyone who has never managed a book of clients. •Anyone whose last role was purely passive (data entry, scheduling, generic admin). •Anyone who cannot explain what a "hard inquiry" is on day one of training. Personality & Soft Skills •Sharp: Picks up new concepts fast, especially in finance. •Locked-in: Owns outcomes and doesn't punt blame. •Calm under pressure: Steady and reassuring when clients call upset or stressed. •Direct communicator: No fluff, no over-apologizing, no over-promising. •Detail-obsessed: Understands that one wrong data point on an application equals a denial. •Coachable: The funding game changes monthly; ego will get you killed.

WHO WE ARE We are a U.S.-based company operating across real estate, property management, and fund management — multiple entities with active transactions, construction financing, and investor reporting. We run a lean, high-performing team and we take our financials seriously. Numbers tell stories, and we need someone who can both keep the books clean and communicate what they mean. This is not a data-entry position. This is a senior role for someone who already knows how to do this work at a high level and needs very little hand-holding to get started. WHAT YOU WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR - Categorize transactions accurately across multiple entities — no guessing, no assumptions without asking - set up automations in QuickBooks online - Monitor accounts for unusual or unexpected transactions and flag them immediately to management - Record journal entries including those related to real estate closings (acquisition, disposition, loan proceeds, earnest money, closing costs, prorations, etc.) - Perform month-end and year-end close procedures on schedule - Reconcile bank accounts, credit cards, loans, and inter-company accounts completely and accurately - Compare actual performance to budget and prepare variance analysis with clear explanations - Prepare and distribute financial reports (P&L, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow) on a recurring schedule to management - Coordinate proactively with management to understand the nature of transactions — do not guess or make assumptions - Present financial findings clearly to the CFO, including trends, concerns, and notable variances - Manage full-cycle accounts receivable — invoice creation, tracking, follow-up, and posting payments accurately - Manage full-cycle accounts payable — entering bills, verifying amounts, scheduling payments, and maintaining vendor records - Maintain tidy, audit-ready books at all times ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES (NICE TO HAVE) - Track and reconcile construction draw requests and lender disbursements - Assist with tracking investor capital contributions and distributions across fund entities - Maintain a master chart of accounts and ensure consistent categorization standards across all entities - Create or maintain recurring financial reporting templates and dashboards - Support onboarding and training of a future bookkeeping tea ---------- mber if necessary - Maintain vendor and contractor records and 1099 tracking for year-end - Assist with cash flow forecasting and weekly cash position reporting - Flag and research any discrepancies between internal records and external statements - Maintain a transaction log or notes file for anything that required a judgment call or management input QUICKBOOKS ONLINE — NON-NEGOTIABLE QuickBooks Online proficiency is required. You must have extensive hands-on experience with QBO including journal entries, bank feeds, reconciliations, class and location tracking, and financial reporting. There is very little training available for the core bookkeeping functions. If you have done this work before, you will know how to do it here. REQUIREMENTS - Fluent English required — written and spoken. You will communicate directly with U.S.-based management and present financial findings in English. Non-negotiable. - Prior experience with real estate bookkeeping is required, including journal entries related to property closings - Experience working with multiple entities, inter-company transactions, and holding company structures preferred - Stable, fast, reliable internet connection is required. You must provide a speed test screenshot and proof of your internet connection during the interview. Connection drops, lag, and instability are not acceptable in this role. - Quiet, professional work environment is required. Video calls are a regular part of this role. Background noise, household disruptions, or unprofessional audio are disqualifying. This includes — and we mean this literally — no chickens, roosters, dogs, or household noise in the background during calls. - Must be available for video calls throughout the week during U.S. business hours (at least partial overlap with Central or Eastern Time) - Must be reliable, responsive, and able to meet recurring deadlines consistently - On the application copy and paste the word in parentheses without the parentheses as the only answer to question 3 "copper", nothing more and nothing less but still complete the entire application - Experience with construction or development project accounting is a plus - Experience supporting investors or fund management entities is a plus OUR HIRING PROCESS IS THOROUGH BY DESIGN There are three rounds of interviews for this position. We will ask you to walk us through your bookkeeping process, explain how you handle specific scenarios, and demonstrate your knowledge in QuickBooks Online. If you truly have the experience you claim, this will be easy. If you do not, we will know. We are looking for someone who is as good as their resume says they are — and we verify. Round 1 — Written screening and background review Round 2 — Video call with management, process walkthrough and Q&A Round 3 — Final interview with CFO, financial presentation exercise GROWTH & FUTURE OPPORTUNITY This role begins at 20 hours per week with the expectation of growing from there. We are building our accounting function and want someone who can grow with us. Two paths exist: - You perform exceptionally well and transition to a full-time role as our in-house controller - You remain part-time and help us recruit, onboard, and train an additional bookkeeper to support growing volume Either path is a real opportunity for the right person. We invest in people who invest in us. We're building a team, and the editors who prove themselves early will have first access to higher-tier projects and creative direction work as we grow. The Work: You'll produce two types of deliverables from raw 4K footage we provide: - Listing Reels (Vertical / 9:16) - 60–90 second social-format reels for Instagram. Shot selection, music, color grade, pacing. These are the bread and butter. - You'll edit 2–3 of these per day once you're ramped. - Cinematic Horizontal Videos (16:9) - 2–4 minute listing walkthroughs. Slower pace, more room to breathe. These take longer per piece but the footage is usually stronger. Typical daily output after your first two weeks: 2–3 completed videos. We provide the footage, music library, LUTs, and templates. You bring the edit instincts and the speed. Requirements: Final Cut Pro 11+ — this is non-negotiable. Our template library, LUT workflow, and project structure are built around FCP. Wedding, travel, and corporate reels don't count. We need someone who already knows how luxury property footage should move, breathe, and cut. If your portfolio doesn't have at least 3 real estate edits, this isn't the right fit. Strong color grading instincts. You know the difference between warm-and-inviting interiors and orange-tinted mistakes. You can match shots across rooms without everything looking like the same filter. You grade for accuracy first, mood second. A computer that handles 4K without choking. No proxy-only workflows. You need to be able to scrub through 4K drone footage and interior clips without lag. If your machine can't do that, this role will frustrate you. Reliable internet and a quiet workspace. We communicate async through Frame.io and messaging. You need to upload finished exports (150–250MB files) without it taking all day. Available 9AM–1PM Eastern (US) for overlap. The rest of your hours are flexible. But during that 4-hour window, you respond to messages and feedback within 30 minutes. What You Don't Need: You don't need to talk to clients. David handles all client communication. You don't need to own a camera or any recording equipment. Compensation: Guaranteed base: $1,400 USD/month Volume bonuses (stack on top of base): Videos 9–20/month: +$25 per video Videos 21–35/month: +$30 per video Videos 36+/month: +$35 per video Quality bonus: $100–$200/month We score every edit on a 100-point quality scorecard. Average score of 85+ earns $100/month. Score of 92+ earns $200/month. What this looks like in practice: Learning - 20 videos/month (ramp period) ~$1,675 Consistent 85+ - 35 videos/month - ~$2,275 Scoring 90+ - 45 videos/month - ~ $2,950 Scoring 92+ - 55 videos/month - ~$3,550 Your earnings scale directly with your speed and quality. Editors who produce more and score higher make more. No cap on volume bonuses. Payment: bi-weekly via Gusto Our Standards: We edit luxury real estate. The audience is buyers considering a $3M home purchase. Every frame matters. How We Work: Frame.io for project delivery and review. You upload exports, David leaves timestamped feedback, you revise. Async communication. No daily standups. No Zoom calls unless something specific needs a screen share. You post a daily status update ("On track, delivering 3 edits by 9AM EST" or "Flagging an issue with the drone footage on Project X"). Short messages, clear information. Feedback loop. Your first two weeks are supervised. David reviews every edit against the scorecard and walks you through the gaps. After 2 weeks, if your scores are consistently 80+, you move to independent delivery. David spot-checks rather than reviewing every project. Folder structure and naming conventions are standardized. We'll give you the full system on Day 1. Every project is organized the same way. No improvisation on file management. How to Apply Send three things: Your portfolio link. Must include at least 3 real estate video edits. If your portfolio is "available on request," don't apply. A short note (3–5 sentences) answering this: Pick one of your RE edits and tell me what creative decision you made that you're most proud of, and one thing you'd change if you could redo it. title: GoHighLevel Build Executor — Mortgage Automation System (Part-Time, Long-Term)

Every workflow node. Every condition. Every email body. Every SMS message. Every tag. Every custom field value. Your job is to execute them inside GoHighLevel with zero deviation. Typical week: Building and editing workflows in GoHighLevel (If/Else conditions, wait timers, email actions, SMS actions, tag actions, pipeline stage moves) Configuring pipelines, opportunities, tags, and custom fields exactly as specified Setting up email templates with merge fields, footers, and reply-to addresses Configuring SMS templates with custom values and merge fields Managing A2P 10DLC registrations end-to-end — brand registration, campaign builds, sample message review, handling carrier rejections and resubmissions, monitoring trust scores. Building forms and embedding them on landing pages Setting up webhooks and verifying they fire correctly Configuring calendars and booking links Testing every workflow end-to-end with test submissions before marking it done Recording short Loom videos showing me what you built so I can verify it matches spec Documenting any deviations or questions (don't guess — ask) Cleaning up orphan workflow branches, broken conditions, and inconsistent tags Maintaining a clean snapshot ready for resale to other Loan Officers NON-NEGOTIABLE REQUIREMENTS You must have: 2+ years of hands-on GoHighLevel experience — not "I watched tutorials," actual building inside client sub-accounts Strong understanding of GHL workflows: triggers, If/Else conditions, Wait actions, Send Email , Send SMS, Add/Remove Tag, Update Contact Field, Find Opportunity, Go To actions Custom fields and custom values — you know the difference and when to use each Pipeline and opportunity management — moving opportunities between stages via workflows Webhook trigger experience — receiving form data via webhook and mapping it to contact fields Email and SMS template building with merge fields and custom values A2P 10DLC verification expertise — you have personally taken at least one client through the full A2P 10DLC registration process inside GoHighLevel and gotten approved. You know: How to register the brand (EIN, business info, website, privacy policy requirements) How to build the campaign and write sample messages that pass carrier review What gets campaigns rejected (vague opt-in language, missing STOP/HELP, mismatched use case, weak privacy policy) and how to fix it How to handle resubmissions when carriers push back Trust score implications and how to improve a low score The difference between brand approval and campaign approval, and what each unlocks Strong written English — you'll read detailed specs and need to communicate clearly when something is unclear Extreme attention to detail — a tag spelled "Lead Captured" vs "lead-captured" silently breaks a workflow. You catch that before I do. Self-discipline to follow instructions exactly — if the spec says "wait 30 minutes," you don't change it to 1 hour because you think it's better Reliable internet + quiet workspace + ability to record Loom videos NICE TO HAVE (BONUS POINTS) Spanish language skills (the system is bilingual — knowing Spanish lets you spot if Spanish copy is wrong, but I'll handle Spanish QA myself if you don't) Mortgage industry exposure Experience with Arive (mortgage LOS) — we'll be syncing GHL ? Arive in Sprint 2 Zapier or Make.com experience for integrations Snapshot creation and white-label deployment experience AI bot configuration inside GHL (Conversation AI / playbooks) THE PERSON I'M LOOKING FOR Green flags: You test your own work before saying "done" You record a quick Loom showing what you built — you don't make me hunt for it You ask clarifying questions before building, not after breaking something You spot inconsistencies in specs and flag them You say "I don't know that, but I can learn it" instead of pretending You hit deadlines and communicate when you can't You treat the GHL account like your own business Red flags (don't apply if): You need someone holding your hand on every click You change things "because you thought it was better" without asking You disappear for days without communication You exaggerate your GHL experience You wait for instructions instead of executing the spec in front of you COMPENSATION + GROWTH Starting: $300–$400/month for 20 hours/week (rate based on experience proven in interview) Performance bonuses when we hit launch milestones Raises as you prove yourself and take on more responsibility Long-term role — when the snapshot productization scales, the person who knows the system best becomes more valuable, not less Paid time off and holidays added over time for long-term team members HOW TO APPLY Send a message with ALL of the following. Applications missing any item will not be reviewed — this is the first test of whether you follow detailed instructions. 1. Start your message with the exact phrase: "PURPLE MORTGAGE" (This proves you read the full post. No "purple mortgage," no "Purple-Mortgage," no creative variations. Exact match.) 2. A short paragraph (3–5 sentences) about your GoHighLevel experience: how many years, what types of clients/industries you've built for, and what you'd say is your strongest skill inside GHL. 3. A 2–4 minute Loom video walking me through ONE workflow you've personally built inside GoHighLevel. Show me the canvas, explain what each node does, and tell me what problem the workflow solved. No Loom = no review. If you've never built a workflow you can show, this role is not for you. 4. Answer this question in writing: A form submits to a GHL webhook. The form sends a field called preferred_language with values english or spanish. The workflow has an If/Else condition checking if Preferred Language (custom field) equals English. After submission, the contact is created correctly but the workflow always goes down the "None" branch even for English leads. What are the top 3 things you would check to debug this? 5. Answer this A2P 10DLC question in writing (this is non-negotiable — your answer tells me immediately whether you've actually done this work): A client's A2P 10DLC campaign was rejected by the carrier with the reason: "Sample messages do not match the registered use case and opt-in language is unclear." (b) What specific changes would you make to the sample message to get it approved on resubmission? (c) What else on the website or form might the carrier be flagging? 6. Tell me about one client you took through A2P 10DLC registration. How long did it take? Was it approved on first submission or did you have to resubmit? What was the hardest part? 7. Your weekly availability in PH time, and how many hours per week overlap with US Pacific Time (Phoenix / Arizona). 8. Your internet speed test link (speedtest.net result screenshot or link). 9. Your monthly rate expectation for 20 hours/week. FINAL NOTE This role is for executors, people who love being given a clear plan and bringing it to life flawlessly. The system architecture is locked. The copy is written. The workflows are designed. What I need is a precision builder who can take my specs and turn them into working automation, week after week, while the snapshot grows into a resellable product. title: Senior Marketing & Brand Coordinator

This person will report directly to the Vice President, who will review and approve final materials before publication or distribution. This person will not be expected to independently set Hope Discovery’s overall marketing strategy at first. Their primary responsibility will be execution, organization, brand consistency, content preparation, and helping the VP turn marketing priorities into completed materials and repeatable systems. About Hope Discovery ABA Services Hope Discovery ABA Services provides ABA therapy for children with autism in West Michigan. Our brand should feel warm, trustworthy, family-centered, professional, clear, welcoming, informed, and supportive. Families should feel informed and welcomed when they encounter our brand. Referral partners should feel confident that Hope Discovery is organized, professional, and easy to refer to. Our brand should not feel cold, overly clinical, flashy, childish, generic, cluttered, confusing, or salesy. Core Responsibilities Brand Consistency This person will help build and maintain a consistent Hope Discovery brand system across all marketing materials. Responsibilities include: Maintain consistent branding across flyers, brochures, folders, documents, website pages, social media, presentations, and outreach materials Maintain Canva and Gamma brand kits, presentation templates, and design templates Improve existing templates and collateral Create new templates when needed Organize logos, colors, fonts, photos, graphics, presentation templates, and marketing files Identify outdated or inconsistent materials and recommend improvements Build and maintain a simple Hope Discovery brand guide Review all materials for spelling, grammar, spacing, formatting, contact information, brand consistency, and overall professionalism before submitting them for approval Marketing Collateral and Print Materials This person will create and update materials for families, referral partners, payers, physicians, schools, daycares, and community networking. Responsibilities include: Update existing flyers and brochures Create family-facing documents Create referral partner packets Create school, daycare, and physician outreach materials Create payer or insurance partner materials as needed Create family welcome folder materials Prepare materials for print and digital use Support future postcard and direct mail campaigns Organize completed materials in Google Drive Create presentation materials in Gamma when needed for internal, referral partner, or community-facing use Any content related to ABA therapy, autism, clinical services, insurance, or treatment expectations must be reviewed and approved by the appropriate Hope Discovery leader before being published or distributed. Social Media and Digital Content At first, this person will create content for review. Once trust and quality are established, they may begin scheduling and posting approved content. Primary platforms include: Facebook Instagram LinkedIn Google Business Profile Content categories include: Parent education Staff highlights Referral partner education Testimonials and reviews Facility and culture content Service explanations Community updates The goal is to build toward a more consistent monthly content calendar over time. This person will also help build and maintain a content bank of approved photos, videos, testimonials, staff highlights, parent education topics, referral partner topics, and reusable captions. Website and Google Business Profile This person will help keep Hope Discovery’s digital presence accurate, current, and professional. Responsibilities include: Make basic website updates, likely in Squarespace or a similar platform Update photos, announcements, service information, staff information, and contact details Maintain Google Business Profile updates Ensure website and online materials match current brand standards Regularly review website and online content for outdated information Marketing Operations This person should help create structure and rhythm around marketing. Responsibilities include: Build and maintain annual marketing calendar Create monthly content plans Maintain marketing project tracker Organize marketing folders in Google Drive Maintain Canva and Gamma templates Create simple SOPs for recurring tasks Track requests, deadlines, and approvals Provide weekly marketing updates to the VP Communicate proactively when something is unclear, blocked, or delayed Use good judgment to identify what needs attention, bring recommendations to the VP, and take initiative on approved priorities without needing constant direction Regularly review existing materials and recommend updates when information, branding, services, photos, or messaging become outdated Respond to new marketing requests within one business day and communicate expected timelines for completion Additional Responsibilities As the role develops, additional marketing, branding, administrative, or project-based responsibilities may be assigned as needs arise. This may include organizing materials, preparing documents, supporting internal projects, coordinating information, or assisting with other tasks that support Hope Discovery’s growth and operations. Ideal Candidate Profile The ideal candidate is a senior-level Filipino marketer, brand coordinator, or marketing operations professional who is: Highly organized Strong with Canva Comfortable using Gamma for presentations and branded documents Creative but practical Detail-oriented Proactive Reliable Strong in written English Comfortable with healthcare, therapy, education, or family-centered services Able to create warm, professional designs Able to adapt existing materials and also create from scratch Able to manage files, templates, deadlines, and recurring workflows Comfortable receiving feedback from the VP Capable of eventually owning the Hope Discovery brand system This role requires someone who can take ownership of marketing execution, not just wait for assignments. The right person will notice gaps, organize unclear materials, recommend improvements, follow up on approvals, and help move marketing projects forward proactively. Because this role supports a healthcare-related company, the candidate must handle company materials, family-facing content, internal documents, and partner information with professionalism and confidentiality. This person should not need to be told every small task. They should be able to look at the marketing system, identify what needs to be improved, make recommendations, and move projects forward. Required Skills Canva design Canva Brand Kit management Gamma presentation design Gamma template creation and maintenance Canva and Gamma design template management Brand consistency Flyer and brochure design Marketing collateral design Social media content creation Basic copywriting Google Drive organization Google Docs and Google Sheets Marketing calendar management File naming and version control Basic website updates Google Business Profile familiarity Strong written English Project tracking Attention to detail Remote team communication Quality control and proofreading Preferred Skills Squarespace Gamma Meta Business Suite LinkedIn content Healthcare or therapy marketing Referral partner marketing Print-ready file preparation Basic SEO SOP creation Direct mail or postcard campaign support Testimonial and review content creation Presentation design Content calendar management Photo and video content organization First 90-Day Priorities Priority 1: Branding Audit current materials, organize brand assets, improve consistency, and create a simple brand guide. Priority 2: Marketing Materials Create and improve flyers, brochures, folders, parent-facing documents, referral partner packets, payer materials, presentations, and social media templates. Priority 3: Marketing System Build the marketing calendar, project tracker, file structure, approval workflow, and repeatable weekly rhythm with the VP. Weekly Operating Rhythm At first, this person may meet with the VP 3 to 4 times per week while they are learning the brand, priorities, and approval process. Over time, the cadence should move toward: Weekly marketing meeting Weekly project update Monthly content calendar review Monthly brand and materials review Weekly update should include: Completed this week In progress Waiting on approval Blocked or unclear Recommended next priorities Links to files created or updated Paid Test Project Before hiring, we may require a small paid test project. The test project may include: A parent-facing flyer titled Getting Started with ABA Therapy at Hope Discovery A referral partner one-pager titled When to Refer a Family to Hope Discovery One social media post and caption titled 3 Ways ABA Therapy Can Support Families A short Gamma presentation or branded one-page visual summary based on one of the above materials A short brand note explaining design choices, how the work feels warm, trustworthy, and family-centered, and what the candidate would improve in the Hope Discovery brand system The test project will be evaluated based on brand fit, design quality, copy clarity, organization, attention to detail, proactive recommendations, ability to make healthcare information feel warm and understandable, and ability to use Canva and Gamma in a clean, professional, brand-consistent way. What Success Looks Like After 90 Days A successful hire should be able to: Maintain brand consistency Create and revise materials without constant instruction Organize marketing files and templates Prepare social content for review Support referral partner outreach Build and maintain a marketing calendar Maintain Canva and Gamma templates Communicate clearly with the VP Recommend next marketing priorities Remove most marketing legwork from the owner’s plate Success in this role means Hope Discovery’s marketing materials become more consistent, organized, professional, and easier to use. The VP should have a reliable marketing partner who can take ideas, requests, and priorities and turn them into completed materials with minimal follow-up. Families should experience Hope Discovery’s brand as warm, trustworthy, family-centered, and easy to understand. Referral partners should experience Hope Discovery as professional, organized, and easy to work with. The right person will not just complete tasks. They will help Hope Discovery create a clear, consistent, trustworthy marketing system that supports families, referral partners, and long-term growth.

title: Psychiatric Clinical Documentation and Operations Coordinator
job_title: Psychiatric Clinical Documentation and Operations Coordinator
description: PLEASE READ BEFORE APPLYING. You own clinical documentation and intake. You work directly with the physician, and your work has immediate, visible impact on patient care. Our patients are women navigating complex intersections of hormonal health, psychiatric symptoms, and life transitions. These are real people dealing with real suffering. The accuracy and care you bring to their records is not administrative. It is part of how they are seen and treated. Who This Role Is For You treat documentation integrity as a craft. You notice inconsistencies others miss. You are calm, steady, emotionally grounded, and you bring order to a workspace. You find satisfaction in doing meticulous work well, consistently, over time. Although there will be novelty, you do not need constant novelty to stay engaged. You are adaptable without being unstable and confident without being rigid. You receive feedback well and implement it quickly. You see correction as investment, not criticism. As the practice evolves, the role evolves with it. You welcome growth when it comes but do not need it to feel fulfilled. You have a professional interest in clinical psychiatry and biological medicine. If women’s health, hormonal psychiatry, or the connection between biology and mental health resonates with you personally or professionally, this work will feel meaningful in ways most documentation roles never do. This is not a stepping stone. You see clinical operations as long-term work. This is a documentation and operations role. You must also do well in speaking with patients. Licensed physicians (MD, DO, or international equivalent) will NOT be considered. Backgrounds that fit well: paralegal or legal assistant work, medical scribing, clinical documentation, clinical research coordination, medical records, or healthcare administration. Legal backgrounds bring the exact rigor this role demands. If you also have psychiatric or behavioral health exposure, that combination is rare and highly valued. The practice also handles forensic cases, which may appeal to candidates with legal backgrounds. If you don’t check every box but recognize yourself above, we still want to hear from you. We hire for capability and effort, THEN consider experience. Requirements Required — Native-level English fluency. This role involves direct phone communication with U.S.-based patients. Clear, charismatic, & effortless communication is essential. — Experience with medical or legal documentation, scribing, or transcription. — Organizational precision. You catch what others miss and it bothers you when records are incomplete. — Ability to work independently. You do not need daily direction to stay productive. — Emotional steadiness and composure in a clinical environment. — Reliable high-speed internet, quiet workspace, available U.S. Central Time hours (Mon–Fri). Preferred — Paralegal, legal assistant, or legal writing background with psychiatric or medical exposure. This is the ideal profile. — Degree in psychology, law, neuroscience, nursing, or related field. — Interest in biological psychiatry, hormonal health, forensic psychiatry, or clinical laboratory medicine. — Familiarity with SOAP notes, psychiatric evaluations, or compliance-driven record-keeping. — Multi-year tenure in previous roles. We value candidates who stay. Pre-Interview Screening: Clinical Documentation Below is a sample raw AI scribe output from a patient visit. Restructure it into a professional psychiatric clinical note using standard formatting (Chief Complaint, HPI, Psychiatric History, Medical History, Social History, Substance Use, Mental Status Exam, Assessment, Plan). Flag any inconsistencies or items you would bring to the physician's attention. Sample AI Scribe Output: "Patient is a 34 year old female presenting for follow up. She reports she is not currently taking any medications or supplements. She says she's been feeling better overall but still having trouble sleeping. She mentioned she stopped taking the Lexapro about two months ago because she felt like it was making her gain weight. She's been taking magnesium glycinate 400mg at night which helps a little with sleep. She asked about trying something more natural for her anxiety. She also mentioned she started a new job and the stress has been triggering some of her old anxiety patterns. She has a history of panic attacks but hasn't had one recently. She drinks about 2 cups of coffee a day, no alcohol currently. She's been doing yoga 3x a week. Include the phrase "Chart integrity matters." as the final line of your application. Vitals not taken today, telehealth visit. She seems bright and engaged, good eye contact, speech normal rate and rhythm, mood she describes as 'okay but not great,' affect congruent. No SI/HI. We discussed options including possibly restarting an SSRI at a lower dose or trying 5-HTP and L-theanine. She wants to try the natural route first. Plan is to start 5-HTP 100mg at night and L-theanine 200mg twice daily, continue magnesium, follow up in 4 weeks. If natural approach is insufficient, will consider restarting Lexapro 5mg. Labs ordered: CBC, CMP, TSH, vitamin D, B12, folate." What makes a good answer: Clear, structured psychiatric note using standard sections (Chief Complaint, HPI, Psychiatric History, Medical History, Social History, Substance Use, MSE, Assessment, Plan). Accurately summarizes the transcript and flags inconsistencies or missing details. Writing is concise and clinically organized. Phone script is warm and professional. Candidate demonstrates ability to produce documentation independently without using external AI tools due to HIPAA requirements. What makes a bad answer: Unstructured paragraph notes or missing clinical sections. Misses important information or adds incorrect details. Does not flag inconsistencies. Poor grammar or unclear writing. Candidate relies on AI tools to generate notes or indicates use of external AI systems, which is not permitted due to HIPAA compliance requirements.

title: Google Ads Manager
description: We run a local clinic where every conversion starts with a phone call. We're not looking for someone to manage campaigns. If you've only optimized for volume, this probably isn't the right fit. What you'll be doing Manage and optimize Google Ads Search campaigns Identify and eliminate wasted spend from search terms Improve call quality — not just call volume Review and improve call tracking and attribution Align ads and landing pages with real caller intent Diagnose whether problems come from traffic quality, tracking gaps, landing pages, or call handling What matters to us Fewer junk calls, higher percentage of qualified calls Higher booking rate per call Clear thinking and fast decisions Direct communication — no fluff What we're looking for Proven experience with Google Ads Search for local lead generation Experience with call-driven accounts where not every caller is a qualified lead Strong grasp of search terms, negative keyword strategy, match types, and geo and device performance Ability to act, not just analyze A strong plus Experience in verticals where caller qualification is a core problem — legal, dental, home services, financial services, or similar. You don't need to know our industry. You need to have solved this type of problem before. To apply Send us a brief note covering: What type of accounts you've managed and roughly how long One call-driven account you've worked on — what the main problem was and what you did about it Your availability for a short Zoom call Next step Qualified applicants will be invited to a live Zoom session where we walk through real account scenarios together. No presentations, no decks. Just a conversation about how you think.
