We are a small, founder-led business currently travelling nomadically through the Americas. We have a Substack publication, a thousands-strong photo and video library from our travels (Colombia, Costa Rica, Brazil, and more to come), and an Amazon listing with reviews and an established product. We also have an existing Pinterest account with approximately 12,000 followers, currently branded under a previous business name (Working Traveller). Before you start, we will rename the account to This Big World, update the linked website, and refresh the profile. The legacy pins and boards will be left in place - you will audit them, d ---------- which to redirect to new destinations, which to delete, and which to keep. You inherit algorithm trust and an existing follower base, not a blank slate. The Opportunity We are hiring a dedicated Pinterest Organic Growth Specialist to take complete ownership of our Pinterest channel and turn it into a predictable, long-term acquisition source. This is not a "post random pins" role. We are looking for someone who genuinely understands Pinterest SEO, visual psychology, click-through behaviour, and content repurposing - and who knows how to translate those into qualified traffic, email signups, and product sales. You will work directly with the founder, have significant autonomy over strategy and testing, and own the channel end-to-end. If you are currently limited to basic pin posting and account management but know you are capable of much more strategically, this could be a meaningful long-term role for you. Your Responsibilities 1. Daily content production - Publish approximately 10 fresh pins per day, scaling to 15+ pins per day as systems mature. - Work from our existing photo and video library (thousands of travel assets from Colombia, Costa Rica, Brazil and ongoing destinations), plus our Amazon product photography and any blog content from Substack. - Work directly with the brand owner to produce and create new unique content aligned with your keyword research and Pinterest SEO strategy — identifying gaps in our library, briefing what photos or videos to capture next, and suggesting content angles that match what people are actually searching for. - Create multiple pin variations from single source assets — different hooks, different titles, different visual treatments. - Produce all major pin formats: static pins, idea pins, carousel pins, and video pins. - Edit photos and short-form vertical video for Pinterest. 2. Account audit and rebuild - Audit our existing 12k-follower Pinterest account pin-by-pin. Identify which legacy pins still drive impressions, d ---------- which to redirect to new TBW destinations, which to delete, and which to keep. - Rebuild the board structure for the TBW brand (gift angles, destination itineraries, adventure travel themes, off-the-beaten-path stories). - Set up Rich Pins and any integrations between Pinterest and our Amazon listing. - Document a SEO strategy and publishing plan you will execute on an ongoing basis. 3. Pinterest SEO and keyword research - Perform deep keyword research within Pinterest for the adventure travel and gift markets. - Research trends and seasonal search opportunities (Christmas gift season starts in September on Pinterest). - Optimise pin titles, descriptions, hashtags, boards, and metadata. - Build keyword-rich descriptions designed to increase discovery, saves, outbound clicks, and ranking inside Pinterest search. - Treat Pinterest as a visual search engine, not a social media platform. 4. Strategy, testing, and optimisation - Develop scalable pin templates and systems. - Identify winning formats and double-down on them. A/B test hooks, titles, imagery, pin styles, and posting times. - Stay current with Pinterest algorithm changes and best practice. The platform shifts and we need you to shift with it. 5. Reporting and analytics - Provide weekly performance summaries covering pin output, top performers, and any tests in flight. - Provide monthly reports covering: impressions, saves, outbound clicks, top-performing pins, traffic to our destinations, email signups generated, and Amazon sales attributable to Pinterest. - Use Amazon Attribution links on every pin driving to our Amazon listing, so we can measure your impact on actual sales — not just Pinterest's internal click numbers. - We care about real metrics: Substack signups, Amazon sales, and discount code redemptions. Pinterest's own dashboard is directional, not a KPI. Required Experience - Hands-on Pinterest organic growth experience — accounts you have grown yourself, not accounts you have inherited or merely managed. - Demonstrable track record of growing Pinterest accounts from low to high monthly views and outbound clicks (screenshots will be required). - Strong Pinterest SEO knowledge — keyword research, fresh pin strategy, board structure, current algorithm understanding. - Ability to create high-converting pins — strong visual instincts, understanding of hooks, curiosity, and click psychology. - Canva design skills (or Photoshop equivalent). - Short-form vertical video editing skills (Capcut, Premiere, or equivalent). - Experience with Pinterest scheduling and research tools such as Tailwind and PinClicks (or equivalents). - Experience creating multiple Pinterest concepts from a single blog post or source asset. - Confident written English. You will be writing pin descriptions, board descriptions, and SEO copy. - Self-direction. We do not want to micromanage you. We want to brief you and trust you to run with it. - Reliable internet, your own equipment, ability to work 40 hours a week consistently. Bonus Experience (preferred, not required) - Pinterest traffic to Amazon listings specifically. - Shopify or Amazon as a traffic destination. - Travel content experience or genuine interest in travel. - Experience with Rich Pins and Pinterest-Shopify integrations. What We Don't Want xxx  Random pin posting without strategy xxx  Focus on impressions or saves as the goal (these are directional metrics, not outcomes) xxx  Generic Canva templates with no hook, no curiosity, no point of view xxx  Low-quality designs or recycled aesthetics that look like every other travel brand xxx. Anyone who cannot show real traffic and sales results from past work xxx  Agencies, outsourced teams, or middlemen xxx. General social media managers without specific Pinterest expertise xxx Anyone who treats this as a 6-month gig before moving to the next thing What We Offer - Full-time, 40 hours per week, Monday to Friday. - Starting salary: USD $600-$800 per month, with room to grow to $1,000 for candidates who can demonstrate strong existing results. - 13th month bonus. - Compensation increases over time as you prove the strategy and results. - Genuine long-term role with significant upside as we scale. - Direct collaboration with the founder. - Clear ownership of the channel. You have autonomy and you are accountable for results. - Opportunity to shape the role over time - as the channel matures, you may move into a wider growth role. How To Apply This is a deliberately detailed application. We do this because we want serious applicants and we want to filter out copy-paste applications at the start. If the steps below feel like too much work, this role is not for you. Step 1: Send us our application Subject line: "Pinterest Specialist - [Your Name]" In the body of the email , please include: - Brief introduction about yourself. - Pinterest accounts you have personally managed (URLs). - Before/after analytics screenshots showing growth you drove. - 2-3 examples of specific pins you created that performed well, with the metrics (saves, outbound clicks, traffic driven). - Your Pinterest SEO methodology in 3-4 sentences - how you approach ranking in a visual search engine. - Tools you currently use (e.g. Tailwind, PinClicks, Canva, etc). - Your view on the state of Pinterest in 2026 - what is working right now and what is not. - Your time zone, working hours, and earliest start date. Step 2: Test task If selected for the next stage, you will be asked to complete a short test task. This is unpaid and gives us a clear view of how you think and what you produce. Details will be sent to shortlisted candidates. Step 3: Video interview If selected after the test task, you will be invited to a video interview. Step 4: Paid trial Successful candidates start with a one-month paid trial at the full agreed salary. At the end of month one, both parties d ---------- whether to continue. If we continue, this is a long-term role. Why This Role Is Different - This is a genuine opportunity to become the Pinterest growth lead for a growing brand. - We are not hiring someone to manage social media. We are hiring someone to own a channel, build it from an established but neglected foundation, and turn it into a measurable acquisition engine for years to come. - If that excites you, we want to hear from you. We respond to qualified applications within 48 hours.

title: Creative Strategist & Content Producer
description: About the company At Miraco Nutripharm, we are dedicated to advancing health & improving lives. Our goal is to relieve 1 billion people worldwide of pain & discomfort. If you know of anyone who has been worried about or suffered from any health problems, join us in making a positive impact by reducing the pain & distress others have to endure. Job description We're looking for a Creative Strategist & Content Producer to shape how our health & pharmaceutical brands communicate across both digital & offline channels. You'll craft effective strategies that translate scientific credibility into compelling storytelling & creative assets - helping us engage our diverse audience as we expand our presence regionally. The Creative Strategist & Content Producer will be the visionary link between our brand identity, compelling content creation & drive measurable performance across all key channels. This role is responsible for developing & testing high-impact creative strategies as well as producing content assets (visual, video, copy) internally, specifically designed to drive traffic, increase conversion rates, lower Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) & drive overall revenue growth for our Shopify, Shopee & Lazada stores via social media as well as paid advertising platforms. You'll work across multiple channels & markets to plan, create & optimize content that builds awareness, strengthens partnerships & supports the new channels of the business. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys balancing creativity, analytics & brand strategy in the health supplement industry. Key Responsibilities: Creative Strategy - Platform & Channel Strategy: Craft tailored creative strategies for B2C & B2B audiences optimized for platform-specific best practices & formats that align with brand goals & regulatory requirements in each market (e.g., Meta carousel ads, vertical video for TikTok/Reels, static product carousels for Shopee/Lazada e-commerce banner ads). - Hypothesis Generation & A/B Testing: Develop robust creative testing matrices, formulate clear hypotheses for creative elements (hooks, calls-to-action, visual styles, copy length) that drive measurable improvements in Click-Through Rate (CTR) & Conversion Rate (CVR). - Audience Segmentation: Translate target audience data & segmentation provided by media buyers into resonant creative themes, ensuring content speaks directly to different stages of the marketing funnel (awareness, consideration, conversion). - Competitive Analysis: Continuously keep up to date with competitors & industry trends, identifying new & successful creative formats, hooks & messaging to finetune our strategy. In-House Content Production & Execution - Performance Creative Development: Lead the end-to-end creative concept development & production for all organic & paid media campaigns (Meta, TikTok, Google/YouTube, etc.) that align with brand & campaign goals, focusing on high-volume, quick-turnaround testing required for performance marketing. - Hands-on Asset Creation: Directly produce & edit native social content & performance ads using existing assets, stock libraries & internal resources. Static/Image Editing: Adapt product photography, create ad variations & design simple graphics & banner ads iii. Video Editing: Fast-paced assembly, cutting, adding text overlays, music & effects for short-form, vertical video (UGC-style, product demos, testimonials) - Copywriting: Develop high-converting ad copy, landing page headlines & social media captions that align with the creative strategy & brand voice, with a focus on clear value propositions & strong CTAs. - Asset Management: Ensure all campaign assets are correctly tagged, archived & deployed across relevant channels (Shopify, Shopee, Lazada store fronts & advertising platforms). - Testing & Optimization: apply insights & analytics to refine & optimize content effectiveness across platforms. Build 10 landing pages per month based on briefs we provide Design each page to match our brand aesthetic Implement copy, images, testimonials, comparison tables, badges, CTAs as briefed Ensure mobile responsiveness (this is non-negotiable — 70% of our traffic is mobile) Optimise for page speed (Core Web Vitals — we need PageSpeed scores above 80) Make revisions based on our feedback within 24–48 hours Occasionally A/B test variants of high-performing pages What You Need to Have Must-haves: 3+ years building landing pages for DTC e-commerce brands (not corporate sites, not SaaS) Strong portfolio showing advertorial, comparison, and review-style landing pages — please send links, not just screenshots Expert-level skill in at least one of: Shopify (custom Liquid + sections), Replo, Unbounce, Webflow, or Pagefly Solid understanding of conversion principles — above-the-fold hierarchy, social proof placement, friction reduction, CTA testing Experience installing Meta Pixel, Google Ads conversion tags, and GA4 events Good design eye (you don't need to be a designer, but you need to know what good looks like) Reliable communication — fluent written English, responds within 24 hours on weekdays Bonus points: Have built pages for skincare, supplements, beauty, or wellness brands Understanding of Australian market or consumer behaviour Familiarity with split-testing tools (Convert, VWO, Shopify A/B test apps) Experience with TripleWhale, Northbeam, or other DTC attribution tools Have built winning ad creative landing pages that scaled to $1k+/day in ad spend Our Brand Context (read this carefully) Our customers are typically women aged 50+ who've started noticing changes in their body or their parent's. Rate to be agreed based on your portfolio and the complexity of each page type. Bonus for a page that converts Indicative rates (open to negotiation based on portfolio): $50–$75 AUD per page depending on complexity (advertorials and quiz funnels at the higher end; standard PDPs at the lower end). Long-term, reliable workload for the right builder. How to Apply To stand out, please send: 3 examples of landing pages you've built for DTC brands — links only, not screenshots One example of an advertorial or comparison-style page you've built (if you have one) A short answer to this question: "What's the single biggest mistake you see DTC brands make on their landing pages?" Your rate range for these page types Your time zone and weekly availability Please don't send generic templates or "Dear sir/madam" applications — we won't read them. We're looking for someone with strong opinions about landing page design who wants ongoing work with a growing brand.

title: Paid Media Specialist — Google & Microsoft Ads
job_title: Paid Media Specialist — Google & Microsoft Ads
description: What You Will Do Campaign Management & Optimization — Manage Google Ads campaigns across Search, Shopping, Performance Max, and Demand Gen — Manage Microsoft Ads campaigns with increasing scope as accounts are onboarded — Build, maintain, and expand negative keyword lists (from ~100 to 500–2,000+ per account) — Perform weekly search term analysis to identify waste, close variant bleed, and new keyword opportunities — Suppress zero-conversion products in Shopping feeds and optimize product-level bids — Execute device, geographic, audience, and ad schedule bid adjustments backed by data — Consolidate RSA ad copy, remove outdated messaging, and test new creative variations — Manage cross-brand and cross-campaign overlap to prevent self-competition on shared terms Conversion Tracking & Measurement — Monitor and troubleshoot conversion tracking across Google Ads, GA4, Google Tag Manager, and CRM integrations (Salesforce) — Ensure GCLID, GBRAID, and WBRAID parameters are capturing properly across all web forms — Validate that conversion actions are active, correctly attributed, and properly categorized (Primary vs. Secondary) — Track Enhanced Conversions, Customer Match audiences, and offline conversion imports for data quality — Implement and maintain call tracking (Dynamic Number Insertion) and form submission tracking Analysis & Reporting — Produce regular performance reports covering spend, ROAS, conversion volume, cost-per-conversion, and impression share — Analyze campaign, ad group, keyword, product, landing page, device, and geographic performance to surface actionable insights — Document analysis and recommendations in writing before presenting to the founder for approval — Monitor competitive metrics (impression share, overlap rate, outranking share) and flag shifts — Identify landing page quality gaps and coordinate with the team on page-level improvements Account Growth & Expansion — Support Performance Max campaign reactivation and testing with proper asset groups and conversion signals — Build and manage remarketing and audience strategies across Google and Microsoft — Identify impression share expansion opportunities and model incremental revenue impact — Assist with onboarding new client accounts into the paid media workflow as the agency grows What This Role Is Not — Not an SEO, social media, or content marketing role — Not a general virtual assistant or admin role — Not client-facing account management (founder handles client communication) — Not a graphic design or landing page development role — Not an autonomous role on day one — you earn expanded ownership through demonstrated performance How We Work: The Approval Model This is important to understand before you apply. We manage significant client ad spend, and every dollar matters. Our workflow operates on an analysis-first, approval-before-execution model: — Identify — You find the issue or opportunity in the data (waste, underperformance, untapped keyword, bid gap, etc.) — Analyze — You quantify the impact, pull the supporting data, and document your reasoning — Recommend — You present the recommendation to the founder with the evidence that supports it — Execute — After approval, you implement the change and track the result Routine maintenance tasks (search term negatives, bid adjustments within established guardrails, ad copy fixes) will have pre-approved parameters you can act on independently. Structural changes — campaign restructures, budget shifts, new campaign launches, conversion action changes — always require approval. This workflow is designed to protect the client and build mutual trust. Candidates who find this restrictive are not the right fit. Candidates who recognize this as a structured path to full ownership are. Tools You Will Use You must be proficient in the core paid media toolset. Training provided for agency-specific workflows and internal tools. — Google Ads — Search, Shopping, Performance Max, Demand Gen (required) — Microsoft Ads (required) — Google Analytics 4 / GA4 (required) — Google Tag Manager (required) — Google Merchant Center (required) — Google Sheets / Docs / Drive (required) — Google Ads Editor + Microsoft Ads Editor (strongly preferred) — Salesforce or equivalent CRM (familiarity preferred — for conversion pipeline understanding) — Slack (daily communication) — Asana (task management tool familiarity — Asana preferred) Must-Haves — Minimum 2 years managing Google Ads accounts with significant monthly spend ($10K+/month, higher preferred) — Hands-on experience with Search, Shopping, and Performance Max campaign types — Strong understanding of conversion tracking: Google Tag, GA4 events, GCLID attribution, Enhanced Conversions, and offline conversion imports — Experience building and maintaining negative keyword strategies at scale — Ability to analyze campaign data at the keyword, product, ad group, device, geographic, and landing page level and draw actionable conclusions — Experience with Google Ads Editor for bulk changes — Working knowledge of Google Merchant Center and product feed optimization — Microsoft Ads experience (campaign management, import from Google, UET tracking) — Strong analytical skills — you think in ROAS, CPA, and margin, not just clicks and CTR — Ability to write clear analysis summaries and document recommendations before execution — Strong written English — you will present findings and recommendations in writing regularly — Available Monday–Friday with at least 3–4 hours of overlap with US Eastern 9 AM–1 PM — Detail-oriented and process-driven — mistakes on a $1M account are expensive — Reliable internet connection with a backup plan Nice-to-Haves (Not Required, But You Will Stand Out) — Experience managing $50K+/month in ad spend across Google and Microsoft — Experience with B2B lead generation campaigns (not just e-commerce) — Familiarity with Salesforce conversion pipelines and offline conversion tracking — Experience with Dynamic Number Insertion (DNI) for call tracking — Google Ads certification (Search, Shopping, or Measurement) — Experience managing multi-brand or multi-storefront accounts with cross-campaign coordination — Familiarity with landing page testing and CRO principles — Background in agency environments managing paid media across multiple client accounts — Experience with auction insights analysis and competitive share-of-voice reporting Hours & Working Style — Starts part-time: 15–25 hours per week, with a clear path to full-time as you take on day-to-day management and additional client accounts — Long-term engagement — we are building a paid media function inside a growing agency — Consistent daily availability required — ad accounts need monitoring, not sporadic large blocks — At least 3–4 hours daily overlap with US Eastern 9 AM–1 PM for real-time collaboration and approvals — Clear, proactive communication is non-negotiable — if something looks wrong in the data, flag it immediately — You will work alongside the founder (strategy, client relationships, approvals) and coordinate with our SEO and execution teams on cross-channel priorities What We Offer We treat contractors like tea ---------- mbers. After a 90-day evaluation period, you become eligible for the following perks: — Prorated 13th Month Payment — Paid in December or at year-end close, prorated based on months actively engaged after eligibility. — Paid Time Off — 40 hours (5 days) of PTO upon successful completion of the 90-day evaluation period. After one full year of engagement, this increases to 80 hours (10 days) annually. — Sick / Emergency Time — Reasonable notice required. Specific terms defined during onboarding. — Remote Work Allowance — $25 to $50 USD/month to support your internet, power, and workspace costs. Exact amount confirmed in writing based on performance and continued engagement. — Recognized Holidays — Blended Philippine and US holiday calendar agreed upon during onboarding. — Performance Bonus — Discretionary and based on quality, reliability, output, client impact, and role-specific KPIs. — Full-Time Conversion — Strong performers during the evaluation period will be offered a transition to full-time hours with expanded scope and additional client accounts. 90-Day Evaluation Period: The first 90 days are a mutual evaluation period. During this time, we assess reliability, analytical quality, turnaround time, communication, attention to detail, and ability to work within our approval workflow. Contractor perks and full-time consideration begin after successful completion of this period. How to Apply Please start your proposal with the word ROAS so we know you read the full post. In your proposal, please answer the following: 1. You open a Google Ads account and see that Performance Max campaigns are spending 40% of budget at a 1.85x blended ROAS, but the top 5 campaigns averaged 2.77x while the bottom 4 averaged 0.55x. All PMax campaigns were paused by a previous manager. What is your approach? 2. An e-commerce account has only 117 negative keywords and you find $131K in spend on 3,100+ search terms with zero conversions. Walk us through how you would prioritize and build the negative keyword list. 3. Are you comfortable in a role where you present analysis and recommendations to the founder for approval before making changes, especially in the first 90–180 days? If you have case studies, audit samples, or screenshots showing Google Ads performance improvements you contributed to, please include them. We are especially interested in seeing how you think through account problems, not just before-and-after numbers.

description: Job Title: Backlink Outreach Specialist — Performance-Based SEO Role Rate: $5–$8/hour, depending on experience and output Hours: Part-time, flexible — 5–10 hours per week Payment: Weekly via PayPal Location: Remote, contractor role About the Work We're a multi-business marketing agency managing SEO across B2B and ecommerce sites including TriHaz Solutions (medical waste compliance), Plastic Fusion (industrial geomembranes), Bear Brothers Cleaning, The Trade Table, and Sharps Disposal Containers. We're scaling our backlink outreach operation and looking for 1–2 specialists to source and secure quality placements across our portfolio. This is a performance-based role — earnings scale with the volume and quality of links you secure. Top performers move into expanded scopes and higher compensation tiers. This is not a content-writing role. This is sourcing, outreach, negotiation, and securing placements. How It Works You source backlink opportunities relevant to one of our businesses You handle outreach and negotiate terms with the publisher You send us the offer package for approval (details below) Once approved, we proceed and the link goes live and gets verified Backlink Requirements Every backlink we accept must be: White-hat only — no PBNs, link farms, or spam networks Relevant to the business/industry — niche fit matters A new referring domain — not already in our backlink profile Live and verified — we don't accept promised links, only live ones Quality publisher — DR 30+ preferred, must rank for actual industry keywords (not just brand terms) Offer Package Format For every opportunity you submit for approval, include: Website/domain + the exact page where the link will be placed Placement type (guest post, niche edit, resource page, directory, etc.) Price/terms (publisher fee, what's included) Requirements (content length, topic, anchor rules, turnaround time) Estimated timeline to go live What You Bring Existing relationships with publishers in industrial, healthcare/compliance, home services, or ecommerce niches preferred Knowledge of how to vet a domain (DR, traffic, ranking keywords vs. brand-only ranking) Strong written outreach skills Self-directed — we don't hand-feed targets How to Apply Email ---------- with subject line "Backlink Outreach Specialist — [Your Name]" Include: Brief overview of your backlink outreach experience — specific niches and total links built 2 sample backlinks you've built in the past — domain, page URL, and what placement type IQ test result from ---------- /take-the-test/ (free, email ed to you — paste the score in your application) Your PayPal email and preferred contact method If you're a fit, we'll add you to our agency Slack and you can start sourcing immediately. First task: source 2 backlink offers each for ---------- and ---------- to demonstrate fit. Compensation structure is fully transparent and discussed in detail during onboarding.

title: Digital Marketing Specialist — Remote, Full-Time, Trustworthy
job_title: Digital Marketing Specialist — Remote, Full-Time, Trustworthy
description: Who We Are: 1. We're a chemical free cleaning company. We provide cleaner, healthier, and safer chemical free cleaning for families, Moms, seniors. 2. We're aiming for strong revenue growth in 2026 and beyond. That's where you come in. Who We Need: (1) We need an experienced digital marketing professional. Not a trainee. Not someone starting from zero. (2) We need someone who has run marketing projects before. Someone who sets quantified goals, hits deadlines, and measures results. (3) Here's what matters most: your mindset. (4) We live by the optimize — measure — learn cycle. Every project has a number. Every number gets tracked. Every result shapes what we do next. (5) Everything we do is based on trust. You must be able to do the right thing, when no-one is watching. If that sounds like how you already work, keep reading. Are You This Person? 1. Accountable. You own your numbers. You don't blame tools, the market, or the algorithm. 2. Deadline-driven. You hit dates. When something slips, you flag it early. 3. Data-first. You check dashboards before you share opinions. 4. Measurement-minded. You think in baselines, targets, and deltas. 5. Curious. You ask "what's working?" and "why?" every single week. 6. Honest. You say when something isn't working. No sugarcoating, no spin. What You'll Do: (1) You'll run marketing projects that bring qualified leads into our sales pipeline. Real projects. Real numbers. Real deadlines. (2) SEO and AEO (AI Engine Optimization) to drive qualified search traffic (3) Link building campaigns: we need organic, real, and local links. (4) Running email campaigns, by building and improving sales funnels to lift conversion rates (5) Conduct referral campaigns to maximize leads from current clients. (6) Maximize our online reviews volumes through best practices and meet the review volume goals (7) Multi-channel outreach (email , LinkedIn DMs, phone) (8) Running social media campaigns with positive ROIs. (9) Conduct Reddit and Quora marketing campaigns that drive SEO and generate leads. (10) Understand how to track conversions based on marketing channels. (11) Daily, weekly, and monthly reporting on every campaign (12) Supporting sales operations Every project has a goal. Every goal has a number. Every number gets reviewed. What We Expect From You: 1. You carry out marketing projects based on clear goals, timelines, and measured results. 2. You run the optimize — measure — learn cycle on every campaign you touch. 3. After 1 month of training, you hit weekly lead goals, and push to beat them. 4. You report your numbers without being asked. 5. You commit 40 hours per week. 6. We are open for long term contracts. Your Background. You should have: (1) Real, hands-on experience in digital marketing (coursework alone won't cut it) (2) A track record of setting goals, measuring results, and hitting targets (3) Strong writing skills — short, clear, and persuasive (4) Comfort with tools like GA4, a CRM, email platforms, and SEO software (5) A 4-year Bachelor's degree (6) Honesty about what you know and what you still need to learn (7) Growth Path and Pay This role has a clear growth ladder. As your measured results grow, your pay grows. Trainee (Foundation Level) — $6/hour minimum Level 1 (Entry Professional) — $7/hour minimum Level 2 (Intermediate Specialist) — $8/hour minimum Level 3 (Advanced Specialist) — $9/hour minimum Level 4 (Master Marketer) — $11/hour minimum Level 5 (Authority Expert) — $13/hour minimum Level 6 (Lead Manager) — $15/hour minimum Level 7 (Leadership roles) — $16/hour + We start most new hires at the lower levels. We move people up based on measured results, not tenure. We're open to both full-time and long-term contract arrangements. If you want a role where pay follows performance, you'll like how this works. If you want a fixed senior salary on day one, this isn't the right fit. Benefits: (1) AI tools built into everything we do (2) Honest, ethical managers (3) Strong training and development program (4) Clear path to higher pay and more responsibility (5) Real support from the team — including our Recruiting and Training Manager and the company President (6) 6 paid US National Holidays (7) 5 paid personal days accrued in Year 1 (8) 10 paid personal days accrued in Year 2 and beyond Our Culture and Values: 1. Direct, honest, empathetic communication 2. Always learning 3. Good remote work tools 4. Team connection (no one left isolated) 5. Integrity, every time 6. Data-driven, not ego-driven How We Hire - This role matters to us. So we take hiring seriously. Our process: 1. A short survey 2. A work sample 3. A video interview 4. 1st interview on Zoom 5. 2nd interview on Zoom 6. Document review Yes, it's thorough. We're not hiring a contractor. We're hiring a long-term partner who will help shape our startup. This is a small, crazy team. Or a crazy, small team. Works both ways. If you read this and thought "this is me" — we want to hear from you. How to Apply: 1. Ensure your have submit a resume with employment history. 2. List 3 top reasons why you are a great fit. Your turn.

The full list above represents the range of content you may work on over time — not your daily workload. What We’re Looking For Must have: Strong English comprehension — you must fully understand the spoken content you’re editing Creative vision — you can see what a piece could become before you start cutting Editing range across long, medium, and short-form content Audio design skills — music, SFX, mixing, cleanup Personal subscriptions to Adobe Premiere Pro and After Effects — these are required and must be active before you start Portfolio showing technical polish, not just raw pacing At least one short-form vertical example in your portfolio Gets our attention: Experience editing for a creator or brand YouTube channel Can explain what makes a good hook Willingness to work with AI tools (we use ChatGPT and Claude) Experience with video research and B-roll sourcing Nice to have: Familiarity with AI generation tools in Envato or FigmaWeave Experience with Notion and ---------- How We Work Weekly check-ins via Slack to verify workload You own your queue between check-ins — self-managing, not micromanaged Flag blockers within 24 hours — don’t sit on problems If you’re blocked, pivot to the next item in the lineup — there’s always work to pull Respond to leadership on Slack within an hour during working hours Revisions turned around within 24 hours 80%+ of your assets should pass first review with minor or no revisions Expect frequent feedback in the first 60 days as you learn our standards Working Expectations Full-time contractor role, 40 hours/week Work in your local time, but maintain a consistent schedule with a minimum of 2 hours daily overlap with PST Attend one weekly all-media tea ---------- eting (1 hour, during PST office hours) and one weekly 1:1 with your lead (30 minutes) Slack is the primary communication tool — used very often, daily Values — Who Thrives Here You care about the work. You do a second preview before submitting — catching typos, checking audio levels. Not overworking. Just being thorough with the time you have. You take pride in what you produce. You don’t ship work you’d be embarrassed to show. You pursue excellence. Substandard work is not something you can live with. You take the opportunity. LeanScaper is open to equipping you with the tools you need. Take that and push as far as you can go. How to Apply Find our YouTube channel (LeanScaper) and check out the content we have: Then, in your message, include the following: 1. A short introduction of why you should be considered for this role — 2 sentences maximum. 2. Link to your portfolio or reel. Include only samples relevant to this role and that you think will get you the position. Do not send your entire body of work. 3. Links to 3 YouTube videos you think are well-edited and 3 you think are poorly edited. For each video, explain why in 10 words or less. 4. Your expected monthly rate in USD. Applications that do not include items 1–4 will not be reviewed.

title: Client Success & Social Media Coordinator
description: ABOUT FORGE STUDIO Forge Studio is a Melbourne-based creative agency specialising in CGI, film, photography, and digital content for property developers and luxury brands. We deliver end-to-end visual campaigns — from 3D architectural renders and cinematic video through to social media management and brand strategy. Our clients include leading property groups across Melbourne and Bali, and we operate with a lean, high-output team supported by offshore production talent. We’re looking for a switched-on, detail-oriented coordinator to sit at the centre of our client delivery and social media operations — someone who can keep multiple workstreams moving, create compelling content, and maintain the quality standard our clients expect. ROLE OVERVIEW This is a hands-on execution role that bridges client success, social media management, and lightweight project coordination. You’ll be the connective tissue between our creative output and our clients’ audiences, scheduling content, managing approvals, building ad campaigns, and keeping render production workflows on track. You’ll work across multiple clients and platforms simultaneously, using Notion as your operating system, Dropbox as your asset library, and Meta Business Suite as your publishing and advertising engine. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 1. Social Media Content Scheduling & Publishing • Source and curate creative assets from organised Dropbox folders — including photography, CGI renders, video stills, and branded collateral — selecting the right content for each client’s posting schedule and campaign objectives. • Write compelling, on-brand captions for every post, tailored to each client’s tone of voice, audience, and strategic goals. Captions must be engaging, grammatically polished, and optimised for platform-specific best practices (hashtags, CTAs, character limits, emoji usage). • Build and maintain content calendars on Notion, scheduling all creative assets, captions, posting dates, and platform assignments on dedicated client dashboards. Each post should be logged with its associated image, copy, target platform, and status (draft, pending approval, approved, published). • Submit all scheduled content for client approval via the Notion dashboard workflow before any content goes live. Track approval status, implement client feedback, and re-submit revised content as needed — ensuring nothing is published without sign-off. • Publish approved content via Meta Business Suite, scheduling posts across Facebook and Instagram at optimal times. Monitor publishing confirmations and troubleshoot any scheduling or delivery issues. • Maintain a consistent posting cadence across all active client accounts, ensuring no gaps in the content calendar and proactively flagging when new assets or approvals are needed to stay on schedule. 2. Meta Advertising (Paid Social) • Set up and launch ad campaigns in Meta Business Suite (Facebook Ads Manager / Instagram Ads) using pre-approved creative assets provided by the Forge Studio production team or sourced from Dropbox. • Configure campaigns end-to-end: select the correct campaign objective (awareness, traffic, engagement, conversions, leads), define target audiences using demographic, interest-based, and behavioural targeting, set budgets and bid strategies, and assign placements (Feed, Stories, Reels, Audience Network). • Build ad sets and individual ads with correct creative specifications — ensuring imagery and video meet Meta’s format, resolution, and aspect ratio requirements for each placement. • Write high-performing ad copy including primary text, headlines, and descriptions that align with the client’s brand voice and are optimised for click-through rate and conversion. • Implement tracking and attribution: install and verify Meta Pixel events, configure custom conversions where applicable, and ensure UTM parameters are appended to all destination URLs for accurate performance measurement. • Monitor campaign performance daily, reviewing key metrics (CPM, CPC, CTR, CPA, ROAS) and making real-time optimisations — adjusting budgets, pausing underperforming ad sets, refreshing creative, and testing new audience segments. • Deliver regular performance reports to the Managing Director summarising spend, results, insights, and recommended next steps. Flag any issues with ad delivery, disapprovals, or account health promptly. • Stay current with Meta platform updates, algorithm changes, and advertising best practices to ensure all campaigns are built and optimised to the highest standard. 3. Project Workflow Management (3D Renders) • Set up and maintain project dashboards on Notion for active 3D render jobs, using the established Forge Studio workflow template. Each dashboard should track project phases, deliverable status, revision rounds, and key dates. • Receive client briefs, reference materials, and feedback and translate them into clear, actionable production notes for the offshore 3D rendering team. Notes must be specific, unambiguous, and include annotated references where necessary. • Relay revision notes and feedback between clients and the offshore team, ensuring nothing is lost in translation. Track all revision rounds on the Notion dashboard and confirm each round is actioned before moving to the next. • Manage project timelines and status updates, proactively chasing deliverables, flagging delays, and keeping the Managing Director informed of progress across all active render jobs. • Maintain organised file structures in Dropbox for each render project — including source files, reference imagery, client-approved finals, and version history. • Coordinate with the Managing Director on scope changes, additional revision requests, or any production issues that fall outside the original brief. 4. Client Communication & Account Management • Serve as a reliable day-to-day point of contact for assigned client accounts, responding to queries promptly and professionally. • Keep clients informed on content schedules, campaign progress, and render delivery timelines without being prompted — proactive communication is essential. • Manage client expectations around turnaround times, revision allowances, and deliverable scope, escalating to the Managing Director when decisions are needed. • Document all client interactions, briefs, and decisions on the relevant Notion dashboards to maintain a single source of truth across every workstream. TOOLS & PLATFORMS YOU’LL USE DAILY • Notion — Content calendars, project dashboards, approval workflows, task management • Dropbox — Creative asset storage, file sharing, and project folder structures • Meta Business Suite — Organic post scheduling, ad campaign setup, performance reporting • Facebook Ads Manager — Campaign creation, audience building, pixel management, optimisation • Figms — Light graphic design and asset resizing (bonus) • Slack or similar — Internal team communication REQUIRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE • Proven experience managing social media accounts for brands or agencies, including content scheduling, caption writing, and community awareness. • Demonstrated ability to set up, manage, and optimise Meta ad campaigns (Facebook and Instagram) with a clear understanding of campaign objectives, audience targeting, and performance metrics. • Strong written communication skills — you can write polished, engaging copy that adapts to different brand voices and audiences. • Highly organised with an ability to manage multiple clients and projects simultaneously without dropping the ball. • Comfortable working in Notion as a central project management and scheduling tool. • Familiarity with Dropbox for file management and asset sourcing. • Detail-oriented — you catch typos, check links, verify image specs, and double-check approvals before anything goes live. • Self-directed and proactive — you don’t wait to be chased; you anticipate what’s needed and get ahead of it. • A basic understanding of visual aesthetics and brand consistency — you know when an image, layout, or caption feels off-brand. BONUS SKILLS (HIGHLY VALUED) • Basic video editing skills — ability to trim, resize, add captions or text overlays to short-form video content (Reels, Stories) using tools like CapCut, Premiere Pro, or similar. • Graphic design capability — resizing assets, creating simple social tiles, adapting brand templates in Canva or Adobe Illustrator/Photoshop. • Experience with property, architecture, hospitality, or luxury brand marketing. • Familiarity with 3D render production pipelines or CGI workflows. • Basic understanding of SEO, Google Business Profile management, or email marketing platforms. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN THIS ROLE • Content calendars are always populated at least two weeks ahead, with all posts drafted, captioned, and submitted for approval on time. • Meta ad campaigns are live, optimised, and consistently meeting or exceeding client KPIs. • 3D render dashboards are up to date, notes are relayed accurately, and the offshore team has everything they need to deliver without delays. • Clients feel looked after — they know where things are at without having to ask. • The Managing Director can trust that day-to-day operations are running smoothly and only needs to step in for strategic decisions.

title: Onboarding & Listing Specialist
description: We are a short-term rental co-hosting company managing roughly 56 properties across 15 states. We operate under a co-hosting model — property owners retain their listings, reviews, and branding while we handle operations, guest experience, pricing, cleaning, maintenance, and reporting. We compete on quality, not quantity, and we onboard 1–2 new properties per month with a target of scaling to 200 properties by 2028. Onboarding is the foundation of every client relationship. A property that is onboarded correctly generates clean, stable operations for years. A property that is onboarded poorly generates ongoing friction that drains the entire operations team. We are hiring for an Onboarding & Listing Specialist who owns this function end-to-end. Role Mission Take every new property from signed contract to first booking in a defined, repeatable, high-quality process. You are the first operational touchpoint for every new owner and the architect of the conditions under which every other tea ---------- mber succeeds or struggles. Key Outcomes (What Success Looks Like in 90 Days) • Time from signed contract to first live booking: under 21 days on 90%+ of new properties. • Owner satisfaction score on onboarding: 9/10 or higher measured via post-onboarding survey. • Zero listing errors at go-live — amenities, photos, pricing, house rules, and descriptions verified and correct. • Pricing strategy configured correctly on day one — dynamic pricing tools set up with appropriate base rates, seasonality, and event-based adjustments. • Full operational handoff document complete for every new property before go-live — cleaning, maintenance, guest experience, and pricing teams receive complete information. • Onboarding SOP maintained and improved quarterly based on what worked and what broke. Core Responsibilities Owner-Facing Onboarding • Conduct the kickoff call with every new owner — welcome, process walkthrough, expectations, timeline. • Collect all property-specific information: access, utilities, insurance, HOA rules, owner preferences, existing bookings to honor. • Set and manage owner expectations on timeline, pricing strategy, and what they can expect from Divergent through onboarding and beyond. • Serve as the primary contact for the owner during the onboarding period, then warm-handoff to ongoing management. Listing Build & Optimization • Build new listings on Airbnb, VRBO, and direct booking platforms (owner retains listing ownership in the co-hosting model). • Coordinate professional photography when needed; optimize photo order for conversion. • Write compelling listing titles, descriptions, house rules, and amenity tagging. • Verify all listing details against the actual property — amenities present, safety items in place, access instructions accurate. Pricing Setup • Configure dynamic pricing tools (PriceLabs, Wheelhouse, or equivalent) with correct base rates, minimum stays, and seasonality curves. • Identify local events and demand patterns; configure event-based pricing rules. • Partner with the pricing lead on mid-term rental (MTR) strategy when applicable. • Set and document pricing assumptions so ongoing management can adjust as data comes in. Operational Handoff • Document everything the cleaning, maintenance, and guest experience teams need: supply PAR levels, cleaner assignment, maintenance vendors, guest communication templates, property-specific quirks. • Ensure the first cleaning, first inspection, and first supply order are complete before the first guest arrives. • Walk the ongoing management team through the property in a formal handoff meeting within the first 14 days. Process Improvement • Maintain and improve the onboarding SOP — what worked, what broke, what changed. • Build reusable templates, checklists, and automations that reduce onboarding time without reducing quality. • Report monthly on onboarding pipeline, time-in-process, and any bottlenecks. Required Experience & Skills • 2+ years of short-term rental operations experience — hands-on, not adjacent. • Demonstrated experience building or launching Airbnb, VRBO, or ---------- listings from scratch. • Working knowledge of a PMS (Hostaway, Guesty, Hospitable, or OwnerRez). • Hands-on experience with a dynamic pricing tool (PriceLabs, Wheelhouse, Beyond). • Strong written English and excellent spoken English — you will be on owner-facing calls. • Project management discipline — you can manage 3–5 simultaneous onboardings without dropping details. • Comfort with checklists, SOPs, and repeatable processes. Preferred (Not Required) • Prior experience in hospitality, property management, or client onboarding. • Experience with Breezeway, Slack, Salesmsg, and GetClearing. • Design eye for listing photos and descriptions. • SEO or listing optimization experience on major OTA platforms. Non-Negotiable Traits • Organizational discipline. You manage multiple onboardings without letting any slip. • Owner-facing confidence. You can hold a call with a $500K+ property owner and make them feel informed, respected, and confident in Divergent. • Process thinker. You build systems, not one-offs. • Ownership mindset. When onboarding breaks, your reflex is "how do I fix this and prevent it," not "who told me to do this." • Professionalism under owner pressure. Owners can be anxious during onboarding. You stay steady, clear, and solution-oriented. What We Offer • Competitive hourly rate for a qualified STR operator. • One of the most strategically important roles in the company — onboarding directly drives growth and retention. • Quarterly performance reviews with bonus opportunities. • Direct access to the owner (Nick) for strategic decisions. • Long-term role with growth potential as we scale to 200+ properties. • Professional development, coaching, and 1:1 time with leadership. Hiring Process 1. Resume and written application — confirm STR onboarding experience. 2. 2-minute Loom video introduction — walk us through a property you onboarded from scratch. 3. First interview (30 minutes) with Divergent leadership. 4. Paid trial project ($75–100): Draft a 5-step onboarding plan with timelines for a sample property, write the owner welcome email , and identify the top 3 risks for this specific property. 5. Reference checks — minimum 2 written references with specific questions. 6. Owner call with Nick — cultural fit and final decision. 7. 30-day paid trial starts.

title: SEO Specialist
description: SEO Specialist — GWIN HVAC & MRCOOL DIRECT What This Role Requires & What’s Expected The Strategy You’re Stepping Into: We’re building a pillar page + topic cluster SEO structure around the keyword “DIY mini split” to rank #1 on Google and get cited by AI tools (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews). You need to understand and execute this architecture — not learn it from scratch. What You Must Know How to Do 1. Pillar Page Management • Build and optimize a long-form authority page (2,000–10,000 words) targeting a broad head keyword • Structure it with proper H1/H2/H3 hierarchy, internal links to all cluster pages, E-E-A-T signals (author bios, credentials, reviews, trust badges) • Optimize title tags, meta descriptions, URL structure 2. Topic Cluster Execution • Write or manage 10–15 supporting cluster articles, each targeting a long-tail keyword • Every cluster article must bidirectionally link to the pillar — they need to understand why and enforce it • Know the difference between a pillar topic and a cluster topic 3. Schema Markup • FAQ schema, HowTo schema, Product schema • Know which schema types trigger Google features (People Also Ask, Featured Snippets, AI citations) • Work with a developer to implement correctly — not just generate JSON-LD and walk away 4. Keyword Research • Identify head keywords vs. long-tail keywords • Know search intent (informational, commercial, transactional) • Build a keyword map across the pillar and all cluster pages with no cannibalization • Know that we’re specifically targeting unbranded searches competitors aren’t owning 5. Backlink / Paid Article Campaign • Manage outreach to relevant websites for paid/editorial placements • Understand that these links must point primarily to the pillar page to pass authority • Vet domain quality (DA, relevance, real traffic — not link farms) • Track which links are live, where they point, and what anchor text is used 6. Technical SEO Basics • Page speed optimization (WebP images, lazy loading) • Mobile-first layout awareness • Canonical tags, redirect management (singular vs. plural URLs — we’ve dealt with this) • Google Search Console monitoring — impressions, clicks, ranking positions, crawl errors 7. On-Page Optimization • Know the right keyword density (not over-stuffing) • Bold strategic terms in content — but selectively (4–6 max per page) • Optimize image alt tags with 1–2 keywords per image • Write meta descriptions that convert clicks, not just include keywords 8. AI Search Visibility (Non-Negotiable in 2026) • Understand that Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, and Perplexity pull from well-structured, self-contained pages • Know how to write content that gets cited by AI engines (declarative sentences, FAQ structure, comprehensive single-page answers) • Schema markup is part of this — you need to connect these dots 9. Blog / Content Calendar Management • Plan and prioritize cluster articles based on keyword opportunity • Write directly • Know that every blog post needs a strategic internal linking plan before it’s published 10. Analytics & Reporting • Google Search Console — weekly check on rankings and impressions • Google Analytics — track organic traffic, time on page, bounce rate • Report on which cluster pages are ranking and which need work • Track backlink profile growth (Ahrefs or SEMrush) What’s Already in Place (You’re Inheriting) • Pillar page at /diy-mini-splits — partially built, actively being expanded • Several cluster blog articles need to live on the site • Paid article / backlink campaign underway targeting the pillar • Schema partially implemented on product pages • YouTube channel with growing content • Keyword master reference list built out Green Flags to Look For in Candidates • Has managed a pillar + cluster structure before (show us an example) • Understands E-E-A-T and can explain it without prompting • Knows the difference between schema types and when to use each • Has run a backlink outreach or paid placement campaign and can show results • Follows Google’s guidelines — not black-hat tactics that will get the site penalized Hours: Monday: 2pm central -5pm Central Tuesday-Frdaiy 8am Central-5pm Central Pay: Weekly pay on Wednesdays, pay period Monday-Sunday Pay method: WISE Must be okay with screen sharing during working hours

title: Podcast Research VA — List Building for Guest Pitching (No Outreach)
job_title: Podcast Research VA — List Building for Guest Pitching (No Outreach)
description: The Role I'm a 30+ year business owner who has been running a company with my husband, and I'm building a qualified list of podcast interview targets for myself as a solo guest. I need a research-only VA to find and qualify the right shows. This is a defined project, not an ongoing role. The total scope is approximately 200–300 qualified podcasts over 8–12 weeks. If the work goes well and a second research phase becomes useful after my first round of pitches, I'd want to continue with the same person — but I'm not promising ongoing work, and I want to be upfront about that so you can d ---------- if the scope fits you. This is research only. You will not write or send pitch email s, at least in this first round. Your job is to deliver clean, qualified podcast leads in a shared spreadsheet. I'll handle the outreach myself. What I Speak About so you can recognize a fit when you see it, my niche covers: - Couples in business together / husband-and-wife businesses - Spouse of an entrepreneur (the supporting partner perspective) - Long-term marriage paired with a long-term business (30+ year arc) - "Marriedpreneur" / "couplepreneur" life/ "husband-wife business"/ "founders life" - Adjacent: women in business who are married to entrepreneurs, faith-based women in business, family business / legacy I pitch as a solo guest, not as a couple. Deliverable Approximately 200–300 qualified podcasts total, delivered in weekly batches of 20–30 into a shared Google Sheet (I'll provide the template). Each row contains: - Podcast name - Host name(s) - Last episode date (confirmed from the feed) - Recent guest count (out of the last 10 episodes) - Audience signal (Apple ratings count, Listen Notes rank, or claimed downloads — whichever you can verify) - Topic relevance (1 sentence — how my niche fits) - Why this fits me (1 sentence) - Best contact method (email / website form / guest application page / social) - Media-first score (1–5 — see screening section below) - Source URL (Apple, Spotify, or host site) - Notes If you can't verify a data point, write "unverified" — do not guess. Inclusion Criteria A podcast qualifies only if ALL of these are true: 1. Topic relevance — host covers couples-in-business, spouse-of-entrepreneur, marriedpreneur life, OR is a women-in-business / faith-based business show whose audience would benefit from my angle. 2. Activity — new episode published within the last 60 days. 3. Format — interviews outside guests (not solo or co-hosts only). 4. Audience signal — at least one of: 100+ Apple Podcasts ratings, OR Listen Notes Global Rank under 10,000, OR 200+ downloads/episode per public claims. 5. Mid-tier preferred — Listen Notes rank roughly 2,000–50,000. Skip the very top of category charts; I already know those. CRITICAL: Screening for Media-First Hosts This is the most important part of the work. I want shows that are real media properties with engaged listeners — NOT shows that exist primarily as a marketing channel for the host's own paid course or coaching program. The latter rarely book outside guests with overlapping offers; the former are open and worth my time. Use this screening framework for every candidate, in this order: Where to look: 1. Podcast feed and recent episodes — is the show itself active and guest-driven? 2. Host website and bio — is the podcast presented as a standalone media property, or as a support channel for a paid offer? 3. Episode descriptions and guest patterns — do they regularly bring on outside guests rather than teaching solo? 4. Social profiles and pinned posts — does most promotion point to the show, or to their product? Specific checks: - Read the last 5–10 episode titles and note how many are guest interviews. - Search the host's site for the course/program name and compare it to the podcast theme. - Check whether the podcast has a separate landing page or just sits under the course brand. - Scan social posts for the ratio of episode promotion to product promotion. - Look for a free resources page, guest application, or media kit — this usually signals a broader media orientation. Scoring (1–5): - 5 — Pure media property. Almost all episodes are guest interviews. Podcast has its own landing page. Host clearly promotes the show as a show. - 4 — Mostly media. Strong guest cadence; host has a product but it doesn't dominate the show's identity. - 3 — Mixed. About half guests, half solo teaching. Worth pitching but expect more friction. - 2 — Mostly course-funnel. Show is largely solo episodes selling the host's program. Skip unless the host's niche directly maps to mine. - 1 — Pure funnel. Show exists only to promote the course. Do not include. Include 4s and 5s. Mark 3s for my review. Exclude 1s and 2s unless I specifically tell you otherwise. Sources to Draw From - Listen Notes (search by keyword, sort by rank) - Podchaser - Apple Podcasts and Spotify category charts (Entrepreneurship, Marriage, Christianity & Spirituality, Self-Improvement) - Guest histories of specific hosts I'll share with you (after the trial task) - Feedspot directories for marriage / couplepreneur / women-in-business categories Do not pad the list. Quality over quantity. If you can only find 18 qualified shows, deliver 18 — don't invent a 19th and 20th to hit the number. I will check. Trial Task (Paid) Before ongoing work, I run a paid trial: - Pay: $35 flat - Task: Research 10 podcasts using the criteria above, delivered as a filled-in spreadsheet - Turnaround: 48 hours from go-ahead - What I'm evaluating: Quality of fit (did you read my niche correctly?), depth of research (did you find shows I likely don't know about?), and accuracy on the media-first score. The strongest applicant is selected for the main project. Project Scope, Timeline & Pay This project has a deliberately staged structure because the size of this niche is genuinely uncertain — there may be 50 qualifying shows, there may be 200. We'll find out together. - Discovery batch: First 30 qualified podcasts, delivered in 1–2 weeks. This batch tells both of us how deep the niche runs before committing to a larger scope. - Continued research: Based on what the discovery batch reveals, I expect to commission additional batches of ~30 podcasts each, up to roughly 100 total, at the same rate. If the market is smaller than expected, we wrap earlier. - Pay: $4 per qualified podcast - Initial commitment: ~$120 for the discovery batch - Realistic total range: $120–$400 depending on what the research reveals - Quality clause: Pay applies to rows that pass spot-check. Rows with inaccurate data, padding, or that don't meet the criteria don't count toward the total. Be precise; don't pad. - Payment schedule: Paid per batch within 48 hours of acceptance - Communication: Brief weekly check-in (email /loom/zoom-15 min) during the project; async otherwise - Future extension: If a later round of pitches generates good responses and I commission research into adjacent niches, I'd offer that work to the same person first. Required Skills - Excellent written English - Spreadsheet fluency (Google Sheets) - Strong attention to detail — I will spot-check 3–5 rows in every batch. Inaccurate, padded, or AI-hallucinated entries will end the engagement. - Independent research capability - Reliable on deadlines Nice-to-Have - Prior podcast research or podcast guesting experience - Familiarity with Listen Notes, Podchaser, or Apple/Spotify podcast charts - Any background in marriage, family, faith-based business, or women-in-business spaces How to Apply Reply with: 1. Prior podcast research experience (if any) — even one example helps. 2. One podcast you'd recommend I pitch and a one-sentence reason why. This is the most important part of your reply — I read it first. Please do not suggest the obvious top-charting shows. 3. Your time zone and weekly availability. Generic AI-written replies that don't include a real podcast recommendation will be ignored. Looking forward to working with the right person.

description: What This Role Actually Is 4ocean pulls plastic out of oceans, rivers, and coastlines, and turns the story of that work into a brand that customers want to be part of. Social media is how most of the ---------- et us. This role is the daily engine behind that. You take direction from the e-commerce and marketing leads and turn it into posts that go live, on time, on brand, every day. You ideate inside the strategy we set. You build the assets. You schedule the posts. You answer the comments and DMs. You boost what is working and run the simple paid campaigns we hand you. You report the numbers back honestly. We are not looking for someone who waits for instructions on every post. We are looking for someone who runs a calendar inside a clear playbook and makes a hundred small, good decisions a week without needing to escalate them. What Success Looks Like: Three months in, the daily content engine runs without me chasing it. The calendar is full two weeks out. Posts go live when they are supposed to, formatted right for each platform, with captions that sound like 4ocean. Community responses do not pile up unread. Reporting shows up Monday mornings without being asked for, and it tells me something I can act on. Six months in, you are bringing me content angles and trend ideas I had not thought of, and a meaningful share of them are working. Boosted posts and the small paid campaigns you run are improving on basic metrics. You know our audience better than I do on a day-to-day level because you are living in the feeds and the comments. What You'll Do Organic Content Production • Build the short-form vertical video we post to TikTok and Instagram Reels, mostly editing from existing footage, b-roll, and creator content using CapCut, etc.. • Design static posts and carousels in Canva using the brand kit and templates we provide. • Write captions in 4ocean's voice. Community Management • First-line responses to comments and DMs across all channels. Standard responses for FAQs, escalation to customer service or me for anything sensitive, off-script, or PR-adjacent. • Flag negative sentiment, recurring complaints, or PR risks the same day they appear. • Engage with creators, partners, and customers who tag us. What You'll Do — Edit 3–8 minute YouTube videos with clean pacing and strong viewer retention — Apply specific cut, blur, overlay, and graphic notes as provided — Proactively add engagement-enhancing visuals during talking head segments — Deliver first edits within 3 business days; revisions within 1 day — Apply feedback accurately and consistently across videos — Communicate proactively via Slack and email throughout every project Nice to have: Create YouTube thumbnails in Canva · Clip short-form content from long-form footage Non-Negotiables Please don't apply if these don't describe you. — You proactively improve engagement — you don't wait to be told every enhancement — You respond reliably during agreed working hours — You communicate proactively when timelines shift — You want consistent, long-term, project-based work If you need repeat reminders or are slow to respond, this role is not a fit. What We're Looking For — Portfolio examples of educational, talking head-style videos (5–8 min) for entrepreneurs or business audiences — Good editorial instincts — knowing when and how to add visual interest — High attention to detail and a fast-turnaround mindset — Clear, proactive communication Bonus: Experience with thumbnails in Canva · Short-form clips from long-form content · E-commerce or Amazon-related content Compensation & Process Pay is per project and based on the quality of your work. Rates may be revisited after consistency and reliability are established. The right editor will have steady, ongoing work with us. Selected candidates will first complete a short unpaid test edit (30 seconds), then — if we like what we see — a paid full-video test edit. From there, we move to a package-based working arrangement. How to Apply Email ---------- first line must include the word REViVE — applications that miss this will not be reviewed. Include: — 1–2 sentences about yourself and your experience — Links to videos you've edited (talking head style preferred) — Any thumbnails you've created — Editing and design tools you use — Your expected pay range per video — Your typical turnaround time for a 6-minute video — One sentence explaining how you d ---------- when to add extra visuals for engagement The best editors understand the goal of a video and enhance it without being asked. If that's you, we'd love to hear from you.

job_title: Operations & Supplier Management & Customer Service | Custom Merchandise Brand
description: Summary We're a fast-growing Dutch brand making custom branded merchandise for pilates and fitness studios worldwide. Our products ship under multiple labels, manufactured across several factories in Asia. We're a small, ambitious team and we work hard, have fun doing it, and take real pride in what we build together. We're looking for someone who fits that same energy. What this role is This is a Virtual Assistant role, but not the kind where you respond to email s and update spreadsheets on autopilot. We need someone talented, proactive, and detail-obsessed who can own two key pillars of our daily operations without hand-holding: customer service and supplier coordination. This starts as a part-time role of 4 to 5 hours per day, spread across 5 days a week. Our ambition is to grow it into a full-time position as the business scales, so we're looking for someone who wants to grow with us, not just fill a slot. Your responsibilities You start your day with customer service. Our clients are fitness and pilates studios around the world, and everything we make is custom. That means when something goes wrong, context matters. You'll manage incoming email s, triage complaints, and handle them proactively, from first response to resolution. Crucially, you'll assess whether a complaint is valid: did the client receive what they actually ordered and approved? That requires a sharp eye and good judgment, not just a sympathetic reply. Supplier coordination is the second core of this role. You'll be in daily contact with our factories, primarily via WeChat, following up on production status, confirming timelines, and keeping our tracking sheets accurate. You'll forward production orders from our internal team to the correct suppliers with the correct files. Errors here have real consequences, so precision matters. You'll also handle product sourcing when we need it. That means browsing Alibaba, shortlisting realistic options, and presenting a clean comparison, not just dumping links. We want someone who uses good judgment on quality, MOQ, and price before putting something in front of us. On the logistics side, you'll monitor shipments across UPS, DHL, and FedEx, mark delivered orders in our tracking sheet, log costs to our analytics dashboard, and handle DAP shipping admin and customs documentation. What we're looking for Must-haves: - Excellent written English - Available during CET business hours, at least partially - Comfortable with AI tools (this is a requirement, not a nice-to-have) - Experience with customer service and complaint handling - Experience coordinating with suppliers or manufacturers - Highly organised and detail-oriented - Proactive, you flag issues before they become problems - Able to work independently without follow-up Nice to have: - Experience with WeChat, Alibaba, or sourcing from Asian factories - Background in e-commerce, logistics, or operations - Familiarity with tools like Google Sheets, Slack, and shipping portals Show us you've done this We're looking for A-players only. In your application, don't just tell us you're organised and proactive. Show us. Give a concrete example of a time you handled customer complaints, managed supplier relationships, or coordinated logistics across multiple vendors. Generic applications will not be considered. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to complete a short practical assignment before a final decision is made. If this sounds like a role you'd genuinely enjoy and a team you'd want to be part of, we want to hear from you.

job_title: Shopify Ecommerce Operations Manager — Clothing Brand

Pay supplier invoices on a recurring schedule - Monitor Shopify Payments / Stripe payouts and flag anomalies - Maintain our supplier product list CUSTOMER SERVICE - Clear the inbox to zero by 6 PM CET every day with the help of AI - Reply to standard tickets using our existing playbook (AI drafts most replies — you approve / edit / send) - Escalate refund / return / chargeback threats to the founder with a one-line summary - Weekly: report top 3 complaint themes DAILY REPORTING - Update a performance dashboard with yesterday's revenue, orders, ad spend, ROAS - Spot anomalies and flag them by 10 AM every morning META ADS - Track daily ad spend and pause underperforming ads (rule-based — you execute, you don't optimize from scratch) - Brief and submit 1 new ad concept per day to the creative team INSTAGRAM CONTENT (Canva + CapCut workflow) - Post 3 pieces of content per day using our templates - Post and review IG Stories - Scrape and save inspiration from a curated list of competitor accounts - Delete negative / spam comments WEEKLY LAUNCHES - Coordinate weekly product launches: assets ready, product page live, email + social scheduled MONTHLY / PROJECT WORK - Plan one 12-post photoshoot per month - Help recruit additional creative tea ---------- mbers --- REQUIRED SKILLS (must-have, do not apply without these) --- - 3+ years managing a Shopify store doing $500K+/year - Hands-on experience with Meta Ads Manager — you can read a campaign and tell me if it's healthy - Front, Gorgias, Zendesk, or similar CS tool - Canva + CapCut proficiency (we'll see your work in the application) - Excellent written English (you reply to customers) - Comfortable with a Notion-based task system - Available 9 AM – 6 PM CET (Europe time, roughly 3 PM – 12 AM Manila) --- NICE-TO-HAVE --- - French language - Experience with clothing brands - Klaviyo / email marketing --- COMPENSATION --- $900/month for the first 30-day paid trial. Bumps to $1,100–1,300/month after a successful trial, based on demonstrated skill. Plus 13th-month and a performance bonus tied to monthly revenue growth. --- TO APPLY, SEND ME --- 1. Your most recent Shopify store you managed (URL + your role) 2. A 1-minute Loom walking through how you'd handle this scenario: a customer messages at 5:55 PM saying "Where's my order #1234? I want a refund." Talk through what you'd check and how you'd reply. 3. Your salary expectation. 4. The word hello at the top of your reply so I know you read this whole post. Applications without all four will be ignored.

title: Outbound Sales Representative
description: The Role We are looking for a hungry, resilient, and highly articulate Outbound Sales Representative to join our remote team on a part-time basis. Your primary goal will be to generate new business leads and book qualified appointments for our agency by reaching out to UK-based businesses. Commission Structure: 4% per closed web/app project (avg. deal size: £2–3k / ~£80–£120 commission per sale) You will be the first point of contact for potential clients, pitching our web design, app development, and SEO services. Because you will be speaking directly with UK business owners and decision-makers, a neutral accent, exceptional English, and a confident phone manner are absolutely essential. Key Responsibilities • Outbound Prospecting: Identify and research potential B2B clients in the UK who could benefit from a new website, app, or improved SEO. • Cold Calling & Email ing: Execute high-volume outbound campaigns (cold calls, email s, and LinkedIn outreach) to introduce Dorset Tech's services. • Lead Qualification: Ask the right questions to qualify prospects based on their budget, timeline, and technical needs. • Appointment Setting: Book qualified discovery calls and consultations for our senior team to close (or, if you have the experience, close them yourself). • CRM Management: Keep meticulous records of all calls, email s, and follow-ups in our CRM system. Requirements • B2B Sales Experience: Proven track record in outbound sales, cold calling, or appointment setting, preferably within the tech, SaaS, or digital agency space. • Exceptional English: Flawless spoken and written English with a neutral or easily understood accent. You must be comfortable navigating conversations with UK business owners. • Resilience: You must be comfortable with rejection and possess the drive to keep dialing and following up. • Tech-Savvy: A basic understanding of web design (WordPress), SEO, and app development so you can speak credibly about our services. • Availability: Must be available to work from 9:00 AM to 1:00 PM UK time (which is 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM in the Philippines), Monday through Friday. About Dorset Tech We are Dorset's number one web design agency, and we are on a mission to disrupt the web design industry. We pride ourselves on offering the lowest rates in the country without compromising on quality, serving over 2,000 active support customers. We build everything from budget pay-monthly sites to full custom Laravel systems and Flutter mobile apps. Beyond our technical expertise, we are a social enterprise and a carbon-negative company. We power our office with solar energy, drive electric cars, and plant a tree for every review we receive. If you want to sell a product you can genuinely believe in, for a company that cares about its community and the planet, Dorset Tech is the place for you. Probation Period: Initial schedule will be 4–6 hours daily during probation, with transition to full-time expected within 2 months. How to Apply Please apply with your CV and a brief cover letter detailing your previous cold calling or B2B sales experience. Important: Please include a short audio or video recording introducing yourself and giving us a 30-second "mock pitch" of a web design service. Applications without a recording will not be considered.
